title: Soil Productivity by Parcel with NCCPI and CSR2
description: Calculate farmland soil productivity across a field or parcel. Replay an Iowa soil overlay with acreage-weighted USDA NCCPI v3 and Iowa CSR2.
coverAlt: Map of the Marsden Farm study footprint colored by six USDA soil map units, with 13.64 rated acres, a weighted NCCPI of 0.827, and a weighted Iowa CSR2 of 87.33.
coverCaption: USDA soil polygons clipped to the 36 published Marsden Farm research plots. Colors distinguish map units. Plot boundaries from the Iowa State Marsden research team’s MIT-licensed maRsden data.
intro: To calculate soil productivity for a field or parcel, intersect the boundary with the USDA soil map and weight each rating by its acres inside the boundary. In Iowa, use Corn Suitability Rating 2 (CSR2) for the state-specific corn suitability measure. For dryland commodity crops across states, the USDA National Commodity Crop Productivity Index (NCCPI) provides a national measure. Report the rated acreage with the average so a buyer can see what the result covers.
takeaways: Keep the deed or assessor parcel, the field boundary and the land being valued as separate records when they differ.
At Marsden Farm, 13.64 research acres intersected six soil map units. The area-weighted NCCPI v3 was 0.827 and weighted Iowa CSR2 was 87.33.
A soil map unit can contain multiple named soil components. Weight the eligible components inside each map unit first, then weight the map units by acres.
Retain the soil survey vintage, rating measure, boundary and acres without a usable rating.

sections.heading: Which acres should the score cover?

blocks.text: Choose the boundary for the question. A buyer comparing collateral may need the whole legal tract. The operator may need only the field acres going into a crop plan. Record the boundary source and explain exclusions such as a farmstead, roadway or water. If the file uses a traced field outline, compare it with the deed or assessor record before relying on the acreage.

For a mapped soil unit, use the acres inside the chosen boundary. A quick point lookup can identify a soil name or drainage class. Use the polygon intersection to see the share of the site each unit actually covers.

sections.heading: A worked soil overlay at Iowa State’s Marsden Farm

blocks.text: We unioned 36 published research plot boundaries and measured intersections in the EPSG:5070 equal-area projection. This example covers the plot footprint. USDA Soil Data Access returned six intersecting map units from survey area IA015 with a September 8, 2026 survey save date. All 13.64 acres were covered by rated units at the reporting precision. The displayed acres are rounded. The download keeps the precision used in the calculation.

rows: L55 · Nicollet loam, 1 to 3 percent slopes
L107 · Webster clay loam, Bemis moraine, 0 to 2 percent slopes
L138B · Clarion loam, Bemis moraine, 2 to 6 percent slopes
L95 · Harps clay loam, Bemis moraine, 0 to 2 percent slopes
L507 · Canisteo clay loam, Bemis moraine, 0 to 2 percent slopes
90 · Okoboji mucky silt loam, 0 to 1 percent slopes

blocks.text: Nicollet loam contributed 4.83 acres at 0.851 NCCPI, about 35% of the study footprint. The Okoboji unit rated 0.719 and contributed about 0.084 acre. An address or field pin in either unit would return a local rating. The acreage-weighted 0.827 describes the full set of rated plots.

blocks.label: Download the soil map units, component rows and source queries

sections.heading: How to calculate the weighted rating

blocks.text: NCCPI v3 is a relative rating for nonirrigated commodity crops. For the overall version 3 rating, the USDA toolbox uses the component interpretation associated with rule 54955. We used the top-level numeric rating and weighted eligible rated major earthy components by their published component percentages within each map unit. Each unit in this example had one eligible major component with a rating.

For the second weighting, multiply each map unit’s rating by its acres of overlap, sum those products, and divide by the sum of rated acres. Repeat the calculation with the map unit’s published Iowa CSR2. Report the two values separately because each index has a different scale and purpose.

A partial result should carry the rated acres, the total footprint acres and the reason any acreage could not be rated. Keep an unrated unit separate from a soil with a low rating. Preserve the source snapshot and each map unit key so a later reviewer can reproduce the calculation.

sections.heading: What to verify before using soil ratings in a land decision

blocks.text: Compare soil ratings with the acres currently farmed, verified field and yield records, drainage infrastructure, access and any irrigation or water documentation. Check the current lease or farm records for operational evidence. A relative dryland soil rating describes inherent potential over time. Use records for the specific property when you need actual yields or income.

faqs.question: Can I calculate NCCPI for my parcel?
faqs.answer: Use the parcel or field polygon to clip USDA soil map units. Join each unit to its NCCPI version 3 rating and calculate the acreage-weighted average over the rated acres. Save the geometry, source vintage, rated acres and the geometry or records behind exceptions.

faqs.question: What is the difference between NCCPI and CSR2?
faqs.answer: NCCPI ranks soils nationally for dryland commodity crop productivity. Iowa CSR2 rates Iowa soils for inherent corn suitability. Keep the rating scale and source with the result, and choose the measure that fits the decision.

faqs.question: How do I handle acreage without a soil rating?
faqs.answer: Exclude it from the average denominator and report it separately with the reason and the rated share of the footprint. A low rating is evidence about the soil. An unrated area is a coverage gap.

title: Earthquake Risk by Address for Commercial Property
description: Check earthquake hazard by address with USGS seismic design data and local liquefaction maps. Replay two San Francisco checks and download the source queries.
coverAlt: Design spectral acceleration at one second for Site Classes C, CD and D at two San Francisco library address points. Only the Mission Bay Branch point intersects the city liquefaction layer.
coverCaption: USGS ASCE 7-22 design cases using an assumed Risk Category II. The liquefaction check uses San Francisco Planning’s layer. Observations made November 23, 2026 local time.
intro: Start with the building address, then check two different questions. How strongly could the site shake, and is the ground mapped as susceptible to failure during that shaking? USGS seismic design data help with the first. Local liquefaction, landslide and fault rupture maps help with the second. For underwriting, tie both checks to the building’s construction, foundation and retrofit records.
takeaways: Resolve the address to the insured building and its parcel before interpreting hazard layers.
Keep shaking estimates, mapped ground failure and building condition in separate fields.
The two San Francisco points returned Seismic Design Category D in all six design cases. Only Mission Bay intersected the city’s mapped liquefaction layer.
Record the design standard, site class, risk category, map release or retrieval date, and source URL with every result.

sections.heading: How to check earthquake hazard for an address

blocks.text: Use the property schedule, parcel and footprint to reconcile the insured location. An address point can fall near an entrance or represent a whole complex. Compare each building footprint with the local map when the site spans several polygons or sits near a boundary.

rows: How strong is the shaking input?
USGS seismic design or hazard service.
Coordinates, edition or model vintage, output metric, units and all scenario inputs.
Is ground failure mapped here?
The relevant state or local liquefaction, landslide and fault rupture layers. In California, use CGS EQ Zapp for official zone maps.
Separate intersections for each layer, map release, geographic coverage and the feature boundary reviewed.
How might the specific building respond?
Building records, retrofit documentation and engineering reports.
Structural system, vintage, foundation, number of stories, completed work and remaining issues.

sections.heading: Two San Francisco addresses with the same design category

blocks.text: We matched the Main Library at 100 Larkin Street and Mission Bay Branch at 960 4th Street to San Francisco’s Enterprise Addressing System. We passed each address point to the city’s liquefaction layer, then ran USGS ASCE 7-22 with Risk Category II held constant and three illustrative soil classes. These are test inputs for comparison. Confirm the applicable code, occupancy and actual soil class for any real evaluation.

rows: Main Library, 100 Larkin St
Zero intersecting features
Mission Bay Branch, 960 4th St
One intersecting feature

blocks.text: SD1 is the design spectral acceleration parameter at a one-second period, expressed in units of gravity. At the Main Library point, changing the assumed Site Class from C to D increased SD1 from 0.57 g to 1.16 g. The design category stayed D. The letter D appears twice here. One is the assumed soil classification and the other is the resulting seismic design category.

The Mission Bay address point triggered a local liquefaction follow-up even though the design category was the same. For this type of review, resolve the full footprint and consult the current official map. A zero-feature return only describes the intersection test at that coordinate.

sections.heading: What to store when integrating a seismic data API

blocks.text: For a point screen, the Invariant Earth API field seismic_design_category documents its ASCE 7-22 inputs as Site Class D and Risk Category II. Its seismic_pga_2pct_50yr_g field documents a gridded 2018 USGS National Seismic Hazard Model value at a reference site condition. Keep the output names and vintage with the readings. A gridded hazard value at a reference condition answers a different question from a code design parameter for an assumed soil class.

A comparable portfolio record keeps the building identifier, input geometry, each field’s source and retrieval time, and the state of the lookup. Keep distinct results for a returned value, a point outside a mapped zone, an area the source has not evaluated, and a failed lookup. For exceptions, save the document that resolved the gap, such as a foundation report or a completed retrofit permit.

faqs.question: Can I check earthquake risk by address?
faqs.answer: You can screen the address for modeled ground shaking and mapped ground failure hazards. Building-level risk also depends on the structural system, foundations, retrofit work, occupancy and other exposure characteristics. Start with the address point and confirm the building footprint for decisions near a map boundary.

faqs.question: What does a liquefaction zone mean for a commercial property?
faqs.answer: Loose, saturated soil can lose strength during shaking. A zone intersection is a prompt to review the applicable map, foundation and site-specific geotechnical evidence. Check the official mapping and whether an investigation applies to the planned work.

faqs.question: Is seismic design category the same as a loss estimate?
faqs.answer: Seismic design category is an output of a building design framework for specified assumptions. Estimating property loss also requires information about the building, its contents, and how they respond to earthquake hazards.

title: Interconnection Queue Data for Solar and Battery Storage
description: Find U.S. interconnection queue data, verify solar and battery project status, and trace 58 Kern County requests across Berkeley Lab and California ISO reports.
coverAlt: Of 58 Kern County requests active in Berkeley Lab’s year-end 2025 file, 37 were active, five completed and four withdrawn in CAISO’s older workbook. The separate Cluster 15 report listed 11 requests and showed one withdrawal.
coverCaption: Kern County cohort from Queued Up 2026 by Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory and GridTracker, CC BY 4.0. Follow-up from California ISO’s public queue reports. Chart and reconciliation by Invariant.
intro: Use Berkeley Lab’s Queued Up workbook for historical U.S. transmission interconnection requests, then check project status in the operator’s latest report for the relevant study cycle. In Kern County, California, one historical file showed 58 solar and storage requests as active at the end of 2025. California ISO’s November report matched 46. The other 12 appeared in its separate Cluster 15 workbook.
takeaways: Match requests by operator and queue ID. Keep the report date and worksheet with the status.
For a project near your site, confirm the proposed point of interconnection, net export requested and latest study or agreement.
Read solar MW, battery MW and net MW at the point of interconnection as separate fields. A hybrid can list 250 MW for each resource and request just 250 MW of net export.

sections.heading: Where to get U.S. interconnection queue data

blocks.text: An interconnection queue lists requests to connect to a power system. Use the annual Berkeley Lab release to compare territories and recover an earlier view of the pipeline. It covers generation and storage requests seeking transmission connection. Use the serving utility’s own process for distribution connections, and look up large customer loads through the relevant load-service process.

rows: Berkeley Lab and GridTracker, Queued Up
Historical comparisons of requests across U.S. transmission operators. Includes a project workbook and codebook.
Use the original queue ID and archived year-end status, then open the operator report.
California ISO
Individual queue IDs, study groups, reported dispositions and requested MW.
Check Cluster 14 and earlier, Cluster 15, or Cluster 16 according to the project.
PJM
Individual requests and study or agreement documents where posted.
Use the serial or cycle request list according to the project’s track.
ERCOT
Texas generation requests in the monthly Generator Interconnection Status report.
Record the monthly vintage and follow up with the transmission provider for project-specific documents.

sections.heading: What happened to 58 requests in Kern County?

blocks.text: We selected 58 California ISO rows from Berkeley Lab’s year-end 2025 data: 40 solar-plus-battery requests, 12 battery requests and six solar requests. Each had Kern as its reported county and active as its queue status. We matched the operator’s queue ID to each row and checked the county on both sides. California ISO publishes Cluster 15 separately from Cluster 14 and earlier.

rows: Cluster 14 and earlier, run November 23, 2026
37 active, five completed and four withdrawn.
Cluster 15, posted July 16, 2026
11 listed on the Cluster 15 worksheet and one on its withdrawn worksheet.

blocks.text: Two examples show why a dated match matters. Queue 1335 appears on the November completed sheet with an actual online date of July 22, 2026. Queue 2329 appears on the separate Cluster 15 withdrawn sheet with a withdrawal date of July 1. Without the Cluster 15 check, that second request would simply be missing from the legacy report. Keep July’s Cluster 15 listing date alongside those 11 matches when using the results.

blocks.label: Download the 58-request reconciliation with workbook row numbers

blocks.text: The download includes the match decisions, source sheet names, workbook row numbers and file hashes. It preserves missing dates as empty values. This is a follow-up on a fixed year-end cohort. A count of every current request in Kern County would also need newer applications and separate treatment for overlapping reports.

sections.heading: Which MW figure belongs in a solar or storage screen?

blocks.text: The California ISO Cluster 16 workbook lists Airchair 1 under public project number 55357. It shows 250 MW of solar, 250 MW of battery storage and 250 MW net at the proposed connection. The project requests energy-only service and a May 2032 commercial operation date. For a site screen, record the 250 MW at the connection as requested export and keep the two resource figures for equipment and revenue analysis.

Before pricing a battery site, ask for the allowed grid import, discharge limit, charging hours and any curtailment or upgrade conditions in the study and agreement. When comparing sites around the same station, verify the actual bus or line segment. Then check what a withdrawal or later study changed before assuming the site can use the same amount of export.

items.label: Check battery charging and discharge conditions
Check solar land and compare two dated PJM study estimates
Read load headroom and solar export ratings separately

sections.heading: How to evaluate an interconnection queue data API

blocks.text: Give each provider a fixed set of queue IDs, including a completed request, a withdrawal and a request in a separately published cluster. Compare the output with the operator’s original files. Check whether the response includes the study cycle and date, original status, point of interconnection, capacity units and the difference between a requested and an actual online date. A blank should stay blank when an older report or a different project key cannot establish the value.

Use Invariant Earth to assemble the parcel and mapped infrastructure evidence for prospective sites. Attach each operator record to its queue ID and retain each dated observation when the proposed connection or project status changes. Ask for the current study and agreement when the connection drives the price or schedule.

faqs.question: Where can I download U.S. interconnection queue data?
faqs.answer: Berkeley Lab and GridTracker’s Queued Up release provides the historical transmission generation and storage workbook. Check the original ISO, RTO or utility report for the latest information about a particular request.

faqs.question: How do I look up a solar project by queue number?
faqs.answer: Find its operator, then search its published queue report for the project’s study cycle. In California ISO, Cluster 15 and Cluster 16 have separate public reports. Save the operator, queue number, report date and original status.

faqs.question: Can I add solar and battery megawatts to calculate export at the grid connection?
faqs.answer: Use the separately reported net MW at the connection when screening export. California ISO’s Airchair 1 request lists 250 MW of solar and 250 MW of storage with 250 MW net at the point of interconnection. Verify the studied or contracted limit for a commitment.

faqs.question: What does a missing queue ID mean?
faqs.answer: Check the coverage and vintage of the report before recording an outcome. In the Kern County comparison, 12 older snapshot IDs absent from one California ISO workbook all matched another workbook from the same operator.

title: How to Find Building Violations by Address
description: Look up building violations by address or building ID. Compare NYC DOB and OATH data, and verify open status, penalty balances and correction records separately.
coverAlt: Aerial photograph of the Brooklyn Army Terminal buildings and waterfront.
coverCaption: Brooklyn Army Terminal. Aerial imagery from NYS ITS Geospatial Services, 2024.
intro: To find building violations by address, identify the building and the local agency that issued the record. In New York City, search the Buildings Information System and DOB NOW Public Portal, then check the individual summons or violation number. For an OATH summons, read the hearing outcome, balance and correction status separately. In one Brooklyn Army Terminal example, the city’s data returned four summonses marked active with a zero balance on every row.
takeaways: Match the address to a building identifier before pulling a report. A single tax lot or campus address can cover several structures.
Keep an open summons on the review list until you verify its disposition with the city. Record the date that you checked it alongside the result.
Use Invariant Earth to resolve the parcel and check building data. Use the agency’s violation number for the hearing and correction records that belong in the decision file.

sections.heading: How to look up building violations in NYC

blocks.text: Start in the Buildings Information System (BIS). Search by street address or by Building Identification Number (BIN), the city’s identifier for an individual building. Save the borough, block and lot as well. They identify the tax lot for the acquisition or loan file, and New York City Planning’s address tools can list the building IDs on a lot. Check each building that belongs to the deal.

Open DOB NOW Public Portal and search its Violations section by address or BIN. DOB publishes different records in the two portals. Use the original agency record when a result affects a purchase, repair budget or renewal. For a summons, search the OATH number on the DOB summons page and check whether the city accepted a Certificate of Correction or dismissed the case at a hearing.

We used that BIN to query three city feeds on November 23, 2026. The OATH export returned five summons rows, four marked active. Each of those four had a reported balance of zero. The older DOB export returned one dismissed plumbing violation. The DOB Safety query returned zero rows.

sections.heading: What to request before closing, binding or starting work

blocks.text: For a purchase, ask the seller for the original notice, amendments, and proof the issuing agency accepted the correction. For a loan, record which building the exception applies to and who will confirm it before funding. For underwriting, use the notice to identify the system or work involved, then ask for the inspection report and repair documentation. For a renovation, check how the condition affects the proposed work and whether the city recorded completion.

Keep the record type with the ID. A complaint, permit, violation, hearing decision and certificate each answer a different question. Store issue and disposition dates as source fields. Record the date you retrieved the row so a later change in the export can be compared against the original evidence.

sections.heading: How to evaluate a building violations API

blocks.text: Give each provider the same addresses, including a campus and one property with a documented dismissal or correction. Compare the results with the issuing agency’s records. Check whether the provider preserves the original ID, which agency and work types it covers, what its timestamps mean, and how often it checks for updates. For exported statuses, keep the original label alongside any category you assign to it.

Invariant Earth can supply sourced parcel IDs, parcel addresses and the primary building footprint area for location matching. Start there when you have a portfolio of coordinates. faqs.question: How do I check NYC building violations for free?
faqs.answer: Search the city’s Buildings Information System and DOB NOW Public Portal by address or BIN. Search the individual summons number for the OATH record. Use the three NYC Open Data feeds for repeat checks and keep the original identifiers.

faqs.question: Can a DOB summons still be open with a zero balance?
faqs.answer: Yes. Balance, hearing outcome and certification of correction are different fields. The Brooklyn Army Terminal sample returned four rows marked active with a zero balance. Confirm dismissal or accepted correction with DOB when the status affects a decision.

faqs.question: What is the difference between a DOB violation and an OATH summons?
faqs.answer: NYC DOB publishes civil penalties in its older DOB Violations and newer DOB Safety Violations feeds. DOB’s summonses adjudicated by OATH appear in a separate feed called DOB ECB Violations.

faqs.question: Does an empty violation API response clear a building?
faqs.answer: An empty response means that the selected feed returned no matching rows for that query. In the Brooklyn example, the DOB Safety feed returned nothing while the OATH feed returned five records for the same BIN. Check the city’s portals and the other buildings on the lot.

title: How to Check a Commercial Mortgage Release by Address
description: Use NYC ACRIS document and parcel records to distinguish a partial release from a mortgage satisfaction. Compare two Manhattan cases and download the source rows.
coverAlt: Aerial photograph of the Manhattan block at 732 Eighth Avenue, with the present tax lot 4 outlined. The original mortgage index names air-rights lot 9004 at the same address, while the partial release lists part of lot 4.
coverCaption: Current MapPLUTO lot 4 at 732 Eighth Avenue, over USDA aerial imagery via USGS. The outline shows the tax lot as mapped today. The recorder’s index gives no boundary for the released portion.
intro: To check a commercial mortgage release, match the recorded release to the mortgage by file number and verify the property or interest the release describes. In two Manhattan records, NYC ACRIS uses the same partial-release document code. One lists part of the tax lot and the other lists the entire lot. The lot flag describes the property row. A full mortgage discharge requires a separate check of the recorded instrument and title history.
takeaways: Start with the tax lot, then match the mortgage and release through the recorder’s file numbers.
Keep the parcel flag, air-rights flag and document type as separate fields.
Use the recording date to set the cutoff for a dated collateral review.

sections.heading: How do you find a recorded commercial mortgage release?

blocks.text: Resolve the property to its borough, block and lot in NYC. Search the City Register by parcel identifier, then check the document detail for a mortgage, a partial release or a satisfaction. Use the City Register File Number (CRFN), assigned at recording, to follow the instrument references. Review the record image and schedules for the described property.

columns: What to check in the file
rows: Mortgage (MTGE)
Identify the recorded mortgage, the property interests it covers and how it links to later instruments. Treat the indexed original amount as a document value.
Partial release of mortgage (PREL)
Check the property or interest the release describes and which mortgage it references. One released lot may be part of a broader financing.
Satisfaction of mortgage (SAT)
Find the executed satisfaction, the mortgage it identifies and any assignments or other instruments relevant to the recorder’s discharge.

sections.heading: What did two Manhattan release records show?

blocks.text: The index for 732 Eighth Avenue shows a partial release recorded September 18, 2026. Its property row lists Manhattan block 1017, lot 4, with partial-lot code P. The release references the 2014 mortgage recorded as 2014000409510. That mortgage has nine property rows. The row at the same street address lists lot 9004 with air rights marked Y. A join on street address alone would conflate the two identifiers.

sections.heading: Does an entire-lot flag mean the mortgage was paid off?

blocks.text: At 300 Lafayette Street, the release has an entire-lot flag and still carries the partial-release document code. The two labels describe different parts of the record. The index also shows a zero document amount for both partial releases. For a payoff or discharge decision, obtain the relevant recorded satisfaction or other title evidence and confirm the loan status with the holder.

The 300 Lafayette release is dated September 22 and was recorded October 14, a 22-day difference. For a review with a September 30 recording cutoff, that row falls after the cutoff. The extract’s good-through field identifies the extract’s coverage date. A provider’s own first-seen timestamp tells you when the row was available in that provider’s system.

sections.heading: How should a lender test the data on a portfolio?

blocks.text: Use Invariant Earth to resolve the current parcel from an address and keep the match status and source with the collateral file. Join that parcel to the recorder’s document and reference tables. The two cases here use NYC’s published index records for the instruments.

Give the provider the original and current parcel identifiers plus the known mortgage file number. Ask for all references and their instrument types, the exact records behind each release flag, and both the document and recording dates. Include a test in which a street address matches while the lot or property interest differs. Check whether the workflow sends that case to review.

title: How to Find Commercial Mortgage Records by Address
description: Find commercial mortgage records by address. Use NYC recorder data to trace assignments, agreements and releases, and avoid counting the same obligation twice.
coverAlt: Aerial photograph of 25 Water Street in Lower Manhattan with the tax lot outlined.
coverCaption: 25 Water Street during conversion. Cropped NYC OTI 2024 aerial imagery, CC BY 4.0. Invariant added the MapPLUTO 26v2 tax lot outline.
intro: Start with the parcel and recorder’s office. Then trace each mortgage, assignment, agreement and release by instrument number. At 25 Water Street in New York, the recorder indexed a $415 million agreement and a $415 million assignment of leases and rents on the same day in 2025. The rent assignment directly references the agreement. Adding those two rows would put $830 million in the file without evidence of two separate loans.
takeaways: Confirm the parcel identifier and jurisdiction before searching. New York City lists the 25 Water Street property under 115 Broad Street in MapPLUTO.
Keep the document date, recorder date, instrument type and referenced records with each amount.

Use Invariant Earth to match collateral to a sourced parcel and attach site evidence. For a credit decision, verify recorded instruments with the recorder and obtain the appropriate title and servicer records.

sections.heading: How to look up commercial mortgage records for a property

blocks.text: Start with a situs address, the property’s physical address, and resolve it to the tax parcel or legal description. Confirm the match before pulling financing records. The owner’s public filing uses 25 Water Street. MapPLUTO lists 115 Broad Street for Manhattan block 5, lot 10, borough-block-lot number 1000050010. Invariant Earth’s public API describes a parcel ID and parcel address for this type of match. Check whether the coordinate actually sits inside the parcel because the service can return a nearby parcel where there is no containing match.

New York City’s Automated City Register Information System, or ACRIS, covers Manhattan, the Bronx, Brooklyn and Queens. It lets you search by parcel or City Register File Number, known as a CRFN. Join the Legals table to the Master table by document ID, then follow the References table by document ID or CRFN. For older entries, preserve reel and page. Check the recording jurisdiction elsewhere, including the Richmond County Clerk for Staten Island.

sections.heading: The 25 Water Street case and the repeated $415 million

blocks.text: We joined the parcel, master records and cross-references for twelve selected instruments. A December 2022 agreement shows $107,012,127.64. Two separate mortgages recorded the same day show $208,713,753.40 and $99,274,118.96. Those values add to exactly $415 million. The $415 million rent assignment recorded in January 2023 references all three by file number. Among these rows, the assignment adds a record describing security tied to the financing. Treat the three amounts as a reconciliation of indexed instruments and read the agreements for the actual obligations.

rows: February 23, 2015
Mortgage 2015000061069 for $55.65 million and agreement 2015000061070 for $250 million.
The agreement references the new mortgage by document ID and four older recorded instruments by CRFN.
December 28, 2022
Agreement 2022000461985 and mortgages 2022000461986 and 2022000461988. Their three indexed amounts add to $415 million.
Retain all three document IDs. The separate zero-amount mortgage assignment points to five earlier records, including the 2015 mortgage.
January 10, 2023
Assignment of leases and rents 2023000008537 for $415 million.
It references the three December instruments directly.
December 9, 2025
The $415 million agreement 2025000334868 and $415 million assignment of leases and rents 2025000334869.
The rent assignment explicitly points to the same-day agreement. Keep both filings and review their shared financing once.

blocks.text: The 2025 group also contains a termination that explicitly references the January 2023 rent assignment. The city labels the record a termination of the assignment of leases and rents. A mortgage satisfaction or partial release carries a different instrument type and must be tied to the particular mortgage and property it covers. The 2025 agreement and rent assignment are dated November 25 and were recorded December 9. A review of what was recorded on December 1 should preserve that distinction.

The financing arranger separately announced $535.8 million of acquisition and redevelopment financing in 2022. That describes the announced transaction. The three figures above reconcile particular recorder entries. A lender reporting the current principal, payoff or legal priority needs the correct agreement and current confirmation for the period under review.

faqs.answer: Find the official tax parcel or legal description, then search the local recorder’s index. Save the instrument number and link later assignments, agreements, and releases back to the mortgage they identify.

faqs.question: Does an assignment of leases and rents create a second loan?
faqs.answer: The instrument identifies a security interest in leases and rents. Review the agreement or mortgage it references and track the two filings by their separate record IDs. At 25 Water Street, the $415 million rent assignment directly references the same-day $415 million agreement.

faqs.answer: A recorder index can show the amount on a recorded instrument. Vendor balances may be estimates. Use a current servicer statement or payoff letter for the amount due as of the review date and confirm releases with the recorder and title team.

title: Property Tax Delinquency Data for Commercial Real Estate
description: Check commercial property tax delinquency by parcel. Compare annual tax, unpaid charges, lien-sale notices and payoff evidence using a documented NYC case.
coverAlt: Aerial view of Midtown Manhattan with the Empire State Building tax lot outlined in gold.
coverCaption: Empire State Building tax lot outlined using NYC MapPLUTO 26v2 over 2024 New York State aerial imagery.
intro: A commercial tax file can show an annual bill, a quarterly charge balance and a sold lien for the same parcel. Each answers a different question. In New York City’s 2025 sale, one Class 4 lot had a January charge line with a $65,537.44 balance in February and zero in June. The city’s separate lien record shows a $716,516.29 sale. Start with the tax lot and identify which record supports each status.
takeaways: Match the assessor’s parcel ID before looking up a bill, balance or lien. Preserve the parcel ID used by each jurisdiction.
Compare charge balance and grace date in the same dated extract. Distinguish property tax, water and other charges.
Notice lists describe enforcement stages. New York City’s Final Sale file includes 1,270 Class 4 lots, of which 1,266 also appeared in its first Class 4 notice.
Before closing or releasing an escrow reserve, get a current collector record and the applicable lienholder payoff or release through the transaction team.

sections.heading: How to check delinquent property taxes by parcel

blocks.text: Start with the county assessor or parcel API to resolve an address to the correct tax account. Confirm the unit or building separately when a mailing address can map to multiple lots. Then open the collector’s account for that parcel and review the charge type, the tax period, the grace date and the balance as of a specific date. In New York City, the standing account and dated bill show more recent activity than the quarterly extract.

rows: Annual tax bill
The amount billed for the tax year. Use it for the operating and escrow model.
Get the collector’s balances, due dates and payments.
Quarterly charge extract
A dated balance for a specified charge and billing period. The NYC dictionary defines when a charge becomes late.
Compare grace date with extract date. Read the current account for later activity.
Notice or final sale list
The report stage and the listed parcel. The first notice and final sale are separate events.
Get the actual sale date and current disposition from the collector or servicer.
Current account and lien disposition
The latest statement plus any applicable payoff, redemption or release documentation.
Use the closing team to reconcile the parcel, effective date and scope of the documents.

blocks.text: We filtered the NYC Department of Finance list to its 2025 rows with tax class code 4. We counted unique borough, block and lot IDs in each published cycle and checked which IDs appeared in the 90-day notice. The dates below are the file’s publication months. The city records June 3, 2025 as the sale date.

The list records appearance by stage. It supplies no resolution reason for lots absent from a later file. NYC’s Independent Budget Office reports its broader citywide analysis separately.

blocks.text: For commercial tax lot 1022380035, the January 2025 charge line had a $65,537.44 balance at the February 15 extract. The June 8 extract returned zero for the same charge code and period. Separately, the city account records a June 3 lien sale for $716,516.29 under lien ID 202501. The notice dataset lists the same lot in all five stages.

blocks.text: Invariant makes Invariant Earth. Start with Enrich to match a parcel and bring annual taxes into the same file as building and property context. Request parcelnumb, taxamt and taxyear. Save parcel_match, the returned source and the reported year. Inspect field_omissions when a requested value is absent. sections.heading: What to store in a lender’s property record

blocks.text: Keep parcel ID, jurisdiction, tax year, charge code, due and grace dates, amount and currency, extract timestamp, and the source URL. Store notice stages, sale amounts and payoff or redemption as separate events with their own dates. Keep the basis for each value so a prior review can be replayed from the right information.

Use distinct review states for an outstanding balance, an observed sale, a verified resolution and unknown. An empty response can reflect incomplete coverage. NYC DOF documents a gap in its 2023 quarterly charge extracts. Preserve the unknown and obtain a collector or servicer record where the file requires it.

faqs.question: How do I check whether a commercial property has delinquent taxes?
faqs.answer: Match the property to the collector’s tax account, then inspect the dated charge balance and the due or grace date. Check lien and servicing records separately for transferred debts.

faqs.question: What does an annual property tax API field tell me?
faqs.answer: It gives the tax billed for the stated year. Use a dated collector or treasurer balance and any relevant lien records to check what remains due.

faqs.question: What is the difference between a tax delinquency notice and a final sale record?
faqs.answer: A notice records the parcel at a dated collection stage. The final sale file records the sale stage. Confirm the exact event and any later resolution in the collector’s or servicer’s records.

faqs.question: Should I treat a missing tax notice as a clear tax account?
faqs.answer: Keep the status unknown until a source covers the jurisdiction, date and parcel. Check the current collector account and applicable lien evidence for a transaction.

title: How to Check Fire Station Distance and Protection Class by Address
description: Find the closest qualifying fire station and verify hydrant evidence for commercial property insurance. Replay a Seattle case where the road route was 2.4 times the map distance.
coverAlt: Aerial map of Seattle’s Fishermen’s Terminal, the nearby fireboat station, and the 1.21-mile modeled road route from Station 20.
coverCaption: Seattle’s Fishermen’s Terminal and the modeled Station 20 route. USDA NAIP imagery, 2023. Road data © OpenStreetMap contributors.
intro: Start with the insured building and identify the station the applicable rating organization recognizes for that address. Then verify road distance and a creditable water supply. At Seattle’s Fishermen’s Terminal, the closest station point in the city map is a fireboat station. The closest mapped station with a listed engine is 0.50 miles away in a straight line and 1.21 miles by the modeled road route.
takeaways: Keep the building or entrance separately from the parcel pin, especially at a campus or port.
Record straight-line distance and road distance as different measures. Capture the station name and apparatus listed in the source.
A mapped hydrant starts the water-supply check. Record the utility’s documented flow, pressure, and evidence date when the file calls for them.
Obtain the property’s Protection Class from the applicable rating organization or insurer and record the effective date.

sections.heading: What do you need to check Protection Class by address?

blocks.text: Match the insured address to the correct building and likely apparatus entrance. A parcel centroid can send the route to the wrong street, particularly where a single tax lot contains several buildings. Once you have that starting point, keep the public records and the rating lookup in separate fields.

columns: What to put in the file
rows: Responding station
Current station roster and the applicable property-level rating lookup.
Recognized station, apparatus or designation, road distance, and the date checked.
Hydrant and water supply
Mapped hydrant, utility record and any required flow or pressure test.
Creditable supply, test date, flow or pressure measurement, and the source.
Protection classification
The property result from the rating organization used by the carrier.
The classification, the address or building it covers, the provider, and the effective date.

sections.heading: What changes when you check the road route?

blocks.text: We used the Port of Seattle’s published reference point for Fishermen’s Terminal at 3919 18th Avenue West and ranked all 36 point records in the city’s fire station layer by straight-line distance. We checked the apparatus listed in the fire department’s map, then modeled routes from the two nearest station points with a listed engine. The Port’s coordinate represents the terminal. A specific insured building may use a different entrance.

rows: Station 3
The apparatus map lists a fireboat. No road route was modeled for this point.
Station 20
The apparatus map lists Engine 20. The car route measured 1.21 mi (1,953 m).
Station 18
The apparatus map lists Engine 18. The car route measured 1.42 mi (2,293 m).

blocks.text: The Station 20 route was 2.4 times the straight-line distance. The router snapped the station and terminal coordinates to mapped roads, about 19 and 12 meters away respectively. The road figures are from the public car profile between snapped points. Confirm the recognized response station and the acceptable entrance with the rating provider before using the distance in a quote.

sections.heading: Which source should you use for fire protection data?

rows: Invariant Earth
A cited nearest-station name and geodesic distance for a U.S. coordinate. The catalog describes the Overture source and its filtering rules.
Use it for a first pass across addresses. Verify which station the rating provider recognizes and measure the relevant road route.
Washington Surveying and Rating Bureau
Protection Class for an individual Washington property and location report fields for recognized stations and hydrants.
Use the property lookup when the carrier relies on WSRB in Washington.
Verisk Public Protection Classification
The classification program evaluates community fire protection, including response and water supply.
Confirm the classification and rating input required by the carrier for the address.
Municipal GIS and the water utility
Station points, apparatus maps, and source records for fire flow or pressure when available.
Use them to check a disputed location or document water-supply evidence.

blocks.text: The download includes an Invariant Earth request body for the Port reference coordinate. We checked the field names against the live public catalog. The Seattle measurements above come from the municipal station layer and the public router. The Invariant Earth request requires an API key.

sections.heading: How do you verify the hydrant and water supply?

blocks.text: Start with the location report or utility map, then ask for the record that answers the underwriting question. Seattle Public Utilities distinguishes existing flow-test results from modeled capacity at hydrant tees. Keep that distinction when recording the number. Confirm the relevant hydrant or other creditable supply, its status, and the date behind the evidence.

faqs.question: Can I use the closest fire station on a map for underwriting?
faqs.answer: Use the map to locate candidates. Verify the recognized responding station and the road distance for the insured address under the applicable property rating method.

faqs.question: Does a hydrant within 1,000 feet establish the property’s Protection Class?
faqs.answer: The Washington location report tracks the distance to a hydrant as one input. The property classification also considers the community’s protection and the recognized station. Verify the address-level result with the rating provider or carrier.

faqs.question: Why does road distance exceed the distance on the map?
faqs.answer: Road routes follow mapped access, one-way streets, and crossings. At Fishermen’s Terminal, the modeled route from Station 20 was about 1.21 miles, compared with 0.50 miles in a straight line.

title: Air Quality Data APIs for Historical PM2.5 and Facility Emissions
description: Compare air quality data APIs, historical PM2.5 at outdoor monitors, EPA design values, and facility emissions. Reproduce the June 2023 smoke episode.
coverAlt: Chart of EPA daily PM2.5 from June 4 to June 10, 2023 at Queens College 2, IS 52 in the Bronx, and Jersey City Firehouse. The peak on June 7 is 203.5 micrograms per cubic meter at Queens College 2.
coverCaption: EPA AirData daily PM2.5 summaries for three selected monitor series. The chart includes flagged records where the source reports them. June 2023 episode context from New York State DEC.
intro: Use EPA’s Air Quality System for historical observations at outdoor monitors. Use a current-conditions API for a recent reading or a modeled estimate at a coordinate. For a facility’s emissions, look up the inventory and the permit under the correct facility identifier. Invariant Earth helps an address-based review find the relevant monitoring site and multi-year design value, with the source and distance attached.
takeaways: Save the monitor site ID, series code, method, averaging period, local date and event selection with every observation.
A PM2.5 design value summarizes three years using rules for a specific standard. Read it alongside the event history for operational planning.
Look up facility emissions and permits by their identifiers and vintage. A release in tons per year and a concentration in micrograms per cubic meter answer different questions.

sections.heading: How do I look up historical air quality by address?

blocks.text: Find a representative monitor for the address. Check the pollutant, distance and station setting, then ask whether the monitor is measuring the conditions you need to understand. At each AQS site, the parameter occurrence code, or POC, identifies a series for that pollutant. For a daily PM2.5 comparison, use a consistent averaging period and preserve the reported treatment of flagged events.

Canadian wildfire smoke affected the New York area in June 2023. In the AirData file, three selected 24-hour series at Queens College, IS 52 in the Bronx, and Jersey City Firehouse peaked on June 7 within the June 4–10 test window. These were outdoor concentrations at their respective monitoring sites.

POC 4
Included
Queens College 2 · 36-081-0124
POC 24, corrected series
None

blocks.text: The two Queens College records share a site and date. The source labels POC 24 as corrected and gives it a different event field. Keep each row’s own series and method when comparing providers. None means the row has no flagged event in that summary. An event flag and EPA concurrence to exclude a sample from a regulatory calculation are separate records.

blocks.label: Download 75 EPA source rows and the 21 records used in the chart

sections.heading: What is an EPA PM2.5 design value?

blocks.text: For PM2.5, EPA’s annual and 24-hour forms summarize three years differently. At Queens College 2, EPA’s 2023–2025 workbook lists a valid annual design value of 8.1 µg/m³ and a valid 24-hour design value of 22 µg/m³. The 24-hour statistic averages three annual 98th-percentile values under EPA procedures. The June 7 observation describes one day. A site reviewer deciding how to handle smoke days needs that daily history as well as the long-run statistics.

For a parcel review in Invariant Earth, request the exact PM2.5 design-value fields together with their matching AQS site IDs and distances. Check the year, the annual or 24-hour form, and the selected monitor before comparing properties. For a permitting decision, verify the applicable standards, designations and analysis requirements with the reviewing agency.

sections.heading: Where can I look up a facility’s air emissions?

blocks.text: The EPA facility workbook for the 2023 inventory lists about 2.61 tons per year of direct primary PM2.5 emissions for the Newtown Creek Wastewater Resource Recovery Facility in Brooklyn, EIS ID 8038711. That is an annual inventory estimate of releases from the named facility. To assess contributions to outdoor levels at a nearby parcel, use a source-specific analysis with emissions, weather, chemistry and other contributors. The inventory entry by itself supplies no estimate of the facility’s contribution to the June smoke event.

Use the facility’s name and registry identifiers to locate the applicable permit, then check its regulated equipment, authorized limits, effective dates and reporting record. For covered power units, EPA’s Clean Air Markets Program Data can provide time-stamped unit emissions and operating data. Inventory and permit records use different time periods and units, so save both with their original scope.

faqs.question: How can I look up past air quality for a property address?
faqs.answer: Match the address to a representative nearby monitor and retrieve the pollutant series for the requested dates. Check the averaging period, instrument series, station distance and any flagged events. A gridded estimate can provide additional context where monitor coverage is sparse.

faqs.question: Is AQI the same as PM2.5 concentration?
faqs.answer: AQI is an index used to communicate air quality. Concentration is a physical quantity, such as micrograms of PM2.5 per cubic meter of air. Store the pollutant, units, period and index definition before combining sources.

faqs.question: What is the difference between outdoor PM2.5 and facility PM2.5 emissions?
faqs.answer: Outdoor PM2.5 is a concentration measured at a monitor or estimated for a location. Facility emissions are mass released or estimated over a time period. An emissions inventory alone cannot quantify how much of a monitor reading came from that facility.

faqs.question: Do exceptional event flags erase wildfire smoke observations?
faqs.answer: An archive may include or exclude flagged samples in a summary depending on the selected mode. Keep the event-included records for reconstructing observed conditions and verify EPA concurrence for the relevant regulatory use.

title: Water Withdrawal Data APIs, Water Rights, and Site Allocation
description: Compare U.S. water withdrawal APIs, water rights and utility allocation records. Reproduce a Loudoun and Fairfax County watershed query and see what to verify for a site.
coverAlt: Map of Loudoun and Fairfax counties with four shared watersheds highlighted. The USGS API returned 22 overlapping watersheds for Loudoun and 17 for Fairfax. Four appear in both responses.
coverCaption: USGS modeled public-supply withdrawal queries for July 2020. The API returns whole watersheds. County outlines from Census TIGERweb show the boundaries for reference.
intro: Use the USGS Water Availability Assessment API to compare modeled withdrawals across watersheds. For a project that will draw directly from a well or river, verify the applicable water right or withdrawal permit. For a utility connection, ask the supplier for the volume, pressure, connection point and service date it can commit to. Invariant Earth helps tie the site to a mapped water system and basin so the team can request the right records.
takeaways: A county filter in the USGS Data Companion can return whole watersheds that cross county lines. Join on the watershed ID and month before comparing results.
Read the water right or withdrawal permit for the applicable location, allowed use, season and restrictions.
Verify the site’s peak-day demand, instantaneous flow, potable backup and wastewater terms with the supplier before relying on a service date.

sections.heading: How do I get water withdrawal data by county or watershed?

blocks.text: The USGS National Water Availability Assessment Data Companion can return monthly modeled values for a watershed. We asked for the public-supply withdrawal variable pswdtot in 2020 using the county filter for Loudoun and Fairfax. The API returned complete records for 22 watersheds overlapping Loudoun and 17 overlapping Fairfax. Four watershed IDs appeared in both responses with identical values in every month. A HUC12 is a 12-digit identifier for a subwatershed.

The model for this example runs through December 2020. USGS also publishes historical county-level compilations, including 2015 estimates across multiple sectors. sections.heading: What does a water right or withdrawal permit establish?

blocks.text: For a self-supply project, start with the regulator’s current record. Verify the authorized withdrawal location, source, holder, use, quantity and dates. Read the conditions on low flows, pumping, storage, seasonality and changes in ownership or use. Treat a reported withdrawal as historical use for the scope and period shown. Virginia’s reporting and permitting programs collect different information.

At Loudoun Water, FEMA’s 2023 assessment described a conditional Potomac withdrawal under Virginia permit 10-2020. In the scenario without raw-water storage, when flow at the Point of Rocks gauge fell below 1,400 cubic feet per second, the stated limit was tied to Broad Run’s treated discharge the day before. That is an example of how a permit can depend on conditions. Obtain the current permit and any modifications before applying the rule.

Treatment capacity is a separate constraint. Loudoun Water’s 2026–2035 capital plan describes a 20 MGD starting capacity at Trap Rock and describes Phase II as 32.8 MGD in the project text. The project name and planning comments use 32 MGD. Keep both references and ask the utility which design capacity and commissioning date to use. The capital plan records planned work and does not assign capacity to a property.

sections.heading: What water allocation should a developer request?

blocks.text: Ask for the source and connection point by phase, the maximum day and peak instantaneous flow, available pressure, fire flow, and the utility’s start date and conditions. For reclaimed water, get a written allocation and verify the terms for potable backup, including what happens during an outage. For discharge, confirm permitted volume and water quality with the receiving system. A location inside a mapped service area is where to begin the conversation.

Loudoun Water’s 2026 availability-charge guidelines distinguish maximum-day process water from average-day sewer. On an illustrative 100,000-square-foot water-cooled data center, the process-meter factors yield 100,000 gallons on the maximum water day and 12,500 gallons on the average sewer day. They omit the domestic meter. Use the project engineer’s cooling design and the utility’s approved flow and allocation before budgeting or committing to a site.

blocks.text: Invariant Earth is a starting point when the decision begins with an address or parcel. Its public catalog documents the mapped community water system, the origin of that boundary, and the USGS long-run watershed supply-and-use index. Use the matched system and basin to find the supplier, permit records and the relevant local constraints.

faqs.answer: USGS offers historic county-level compilations. The National Water Availability Assessment Data Companion uses county filters to select modeled watersheds. For the Data Companion, inspect the returned watershed IDs and intersection mode before calculating a total.

faqs.question: Where can I check water rights for an industrial site?
faqs.answer: Look up the record with the issuing state or basin authority. Confirm its status, holder, authorized source and use, diversion location, rate and volume, effective dates and conditions. Verify transfer requirements for the proposed project.

faqs.question: What is the difference between water withdrawal and water consumption?
faqs.answer: A withdrawal measures water removed or diverted from a source. Consumptive use measures the part of the withdrawal that is not returned, for example water that evaporates or becomes part of a product. Keep the source’s spatial boundary and time period in the calculation.

faqs.answer: Give the supplier the site boundary, cooling design, peak flow by phase, needed pressure, service date, backup and wastewater requirements. Get the allocation and delivery conditions in writing. For self-supply, confirm the applicable permit and water source.

title: Natural Gas Pipeline Capacity and Site Service
description: Find gas pipelines and operators near a site. Compare posted capacity with firm transportation and check fuel volume, pressure and service dates for industrial or data center projects.
coverAlt: Decatur Lateral capacity case from the March 2026 FERC order. Out of 194,400 dekatherms per day in revised design, precedent agreements covered 181,400, and the order did not report the result of the open season for the extra 13,000.
coverCaption: Decatur Lateral Project design capacity, precedent agreements and capacity offered in a second open season, as described in the March 19, 2026 FERC order.
intro: To find natural gas service for a site, start with the serving utility or pipeline operator. Give them the site boundary, peak-hour demand, daily volume, minimum pressure and target service date. A pipeline map helps you find whom to call. A capacity posting shows the system for a gas day. The service decision turns on whether the provider can deliver at your meter and on which terms.
takeaways: Map the network and identify the serving utility or a feasible direct tap. Ask about the lateral, meter and upgrades.
Read each capacity number at its own location, direction and date. Firm transportation rights have a separate contract and path.
For on-site generation, size fuel from net electrical output and the higher heating value heat rate, then send the operator a peak-hour profile.

sections.heading: How do I check natural gas service by address?

blocks.text: Start with a parcel or proposed building pad. For a local distribution connection, ask the serving utility to identify the nearest usable main and what it can support. For a direct tap, ask the pipeline about the receipt and delivery path, the new lateral and the custody-transfer meter. If the design needs pressure above the delivery pressure, review the compression requirement with the engineer.

rows: Serving operator

Signed utility or pipeline service agreement and construction schedule.

blocks.text: The local delivery question is common even when gas infrastructure is nearby. Ameren Illinois publishes a tariff for certain nonresidential customers whose incremental demand exceeds existing main capacity. The serving utility can tell you which service terms apply to your site.

sections.heading: What can pipeline capacity postings tell you?

blocks.text: Interstate pipelines publish current and historical operating information on electronic bulletin boards. Start with the location identifier, flow direction and effective gas day. A receipt point is where the pipeline takes the gas. A delivery point is where it hands it off. Check the mainline segments and service notices along the path too.

rows: November 11, 2026
November 22, 2026

blocks.text: Both rows are in MMBtu for the effective gas day at the posted Georgia-Pacific delivery location in Ashley County, Arkansas. In these snapshots, the operating quantity is 5,000 above the design field. Scheduled quantity fell by 988, so posted available capacity rose by 988. Preserve the operator’s reported fields and timestamps. A calculation from design capacity would give the wrong answer on both days.

For service next year, check capacity offerings, firm contract records and the current tariff, then ask the operator about your exact receipt and delivery path. Firm transportation gives the contracted priority on that path, subject to the agreement and tariff. The gas supply contract and last-mile delivery still need to cover the same dates and demand.

sections.heading: What did a real industrial expansion require?

blocks.text: In March 2026, FERC authorized Rockies Express to build the Decatur Lateral in Macon County, Illinois, with two new delivery points. The revised design provided for up to 194,400 dekatherms per day. FERC reported two 20-year precedent agreements, covering 144,065 dekatherms per day for ADM and 37,335 for Broadwing Energy. The additional 13,000 came from a revised assumption about pressure loss through the meters. The certificate recorded a second open season for that capacity and gave no result for it.

The order required the operator to affirm that it had signed equivalent firm service agreements before starting construction. A dated underwriting file should carry the order, the delivery point and the status of later filings separately. Ask for the applicable service agreement and proof the promised facilities are ready by the delivery date before treating a proposed gas volume as available to your site.

sections.heading: How much natural gas does a 50 MW site need?

blocks.text: At a net electrical output of 50 MW and an assumed higher heating value (HHV) heat rate of 9 MMBtu per MWh, the generator uses 450 MMBtu per hour. Running at that output for 24 hours requires 10,800 dekatherms. Using EIA’s 2025 national average of 1,037 Btu per cubic foot gives about 10.4 million cubic feet per day. Use the serving supplier’s heat content for a site estimate.

faqs.question: How do I find natural gas pipelines near a property?
faqs.answer: Use the EIA Energy Atlas or a cited pipeline proximity API to identify the mapped line and operator. Contact the serving utility or transporter with the parcel boundary and proposed demand to determine the connection options.

faqs.question: What is operationally available capacity on a gas pipeline?
faqs.answer: It is the quantity a pipeline posts as available at a location or segment for a stated gas day and scheduling context. Check the point, direction and timestamp. Use contract records and the operator’s response for a future firm commitment.

faqs.question: How much gas does a 50 MW generator need per day?
faqs.answer: At an illustrative HHV heat rate of 9 MMBtu per MWh, producing 50 MW continuously for 24 hours requires 10,800 dekatherms, or 450 MMBtu per hour. Use the equipment’s actual heat-rate curve and gas heat content for a project.

faqs.question: What is the difference between firm transportation and firm natural gas service?
faqs.answer: Firm transportation reserves contractual priority to move gas along an agreed path. For delivered service at a site, verify who supplies the gas, the rights on each segment, the last-mile meter, pressure and the date service can start.

coverAlt: BXP occupancy and lease rollover chart as of September 30, 2026. The portfolio is 89.4% occupied and 91.9% leased. BXP’s share of space rolling is 173,483 square feet in the rest of 2026, 1,408,456 in 2027, 2,006,026 in 2028 and 3,306,254 in 2029.

intro: For available office, retail, or industrial space, start with a current suite listing and confirm the delivery date with the leasing team. For a commercial credit or investment decision, start with the dated rent roll and separate signed leases, commenced leases, and upcoming expirations. BXP reported 91.9% leased and 89.4% occupied in September 2026. It attributed that gap to about 1.1 million square feet under signed leases with future commencements.

Use suite-level listings and landlord confirmation to check what a tenant can actually take.

faqs.question: Where can I find available commercial space by address?
faqs.answer: Start with the owner’s or broker’s current suite listing. Confirm rentable area, whether the space is direct or sublease, the earliest delivery date, and when the listing was last confirmed. An occupancy figure summarizes a building or portfolio.

faqs.question: What is the difference between percent leased and percent occupied?
faqs.answer: Read the publisher’s definitions. For BXP, occupied means lease revenue recognition has started. Leased includes this area and vacant area already under signed leases with future commencements.

faqs.question: How do you calculate lease rollover by year?
faqs.answer: Sum the rentable area or annualized rent associated with leases expiring in each year. Divide by the matching portfolio area or portfolio annualized rent when reporting a percentage. Document whether replacement leases, options, and joint venture interests affect the schedule.

faqs.question: Can I compare a city storefront vacancy rate with a listed office vacancy rate?
faqs.answer: First match the use type, geography, observation date, and denominator. NYC’s registry concerns specified storefront spaces. An office series may cover a broader set of floors or buildings and measure vacant square feet instead of storefront counts.

blocks.text: NYC Planning Labs returns borough-block-lot 1000350001 for 32 Old Slip. The city’s PLUTO tax-lot file stores 77 Front Street for the same BBL. The two addresses and the separate coordinates can be carried under one parcel key while keeping each source’s original value.

For a building-level analysis, keep a building ID alongside the parcel ID, and keep leases at the premises level. faqs.question: What is the difference between sale comps and lease comps?
faqs.answer: A sale comp describes what was paid for an identified property interest. A lease comp describes the cost and terms to occupy specified space. Compare each using matching area, dates, and economic terms.

faqs.question: How do you calculate annual commercial rent per square foot?
faqs.answer: Divide the annual rent by the rentable area that payment covers. Label the result as starting, current, or effective rent and keep the expense and concession basis.

faqs.question: Can you use the GSA lease inventory as private-market rent comps?
faqs.answer: Use it as evidence of reported federal lease economics. For a private transaction, check date, building, space size and condition, expenses, concessions and services before making an adjustment.

faqs.question: Why does a deed search show different amounts for the same sale date?
faqs.answer: Look up the underlying instruments and parties. A deed, ground lease assignment, mortgage, or portfolio transfer can have its own reported amount even when they are recorded for the same parcel.

faqs.question: What evidence do you need to estimate net effective rent?
faqs.answer: Start with the actual lease cash-flow schedule, free rent, allowances, costs and the assumed lease term. Record whether the calculation uses a simple average or discounted cash flows, and use the same method across the comps.

title: How to Check Hospital, School, and Fire Coverage by Address
description: Check hospital drive times, public school attendance zones, and fire service providers using separate sources. Compare the records at a Kansas housing development.
coverAlt: Aerial map of the Leawood study area with three modeled hospital routes and a 10-minute drive boundary. The site-area lookup shows Leawood Middle School and Leawood Fire as the county-mapped service provider.
coverCaption: The route model starts at a public junction near Leawood Market Center. The school and fire records were checked at points within the planned site area.
intro: To check hospital, school, and fire coverage for an address, use a road network for hospital access, an attendance map for public schools, and a service boundary for the responsible fire agency. At a proposed 64-townhome development in Leawood, Kansas, Prairie Star Middle was closer than Leawood Middle, the school indicated by the county attendance map. A hospital in the 10-minute drive area also had conflicting emergency-department records.
takeaways: Keep a facility’s location, the services it reports, and modeled travel time in separate fields.
Check school attendance boundaries by grade, school year, and exact dwelling address. The closest campus is a poor substitute for this lookup.
Use county service polygons to identify the responsible fire agency. Check local dispatch and ambulance transport records for details about emergency response.

sections.heading: Which maps answer which community-service questions?

rows: How far is a hospital that offers the required service?
A hospital register, care-specific records, operator information, and a routed trip.
CMS Certification Number, address or entrance, service evidence, road network vintage, and travel assumptions.
Which public school serves a new dwelling?
School district and grade-specific attendance boundaries, followed by the district’s address lookup.
Exact home address, grade, school year, and the district’s assignment result.
Which fire or ambulance agency serves the site?
County fire service areas and the local agency’s standards of cover or dispatch documentation.
Responsible agency, date, and what the source covers, such as first response, automatic aid, or transport.

blocks.text: The worked example uses Leawood Market Center, south of West 135th Street between Kenneth Road and State Line Road. City Ordinance 3210 approved the rezoning and preliminary plan on May 18, 2026. The staff report describes 64 proposed townhomes across the residential part of the plan. For the lookup we tested three reference points within the area shown on the filed plan. The hospital routes begin at the nearby public junction of Kenneth Road and West 137th Street.

blocks.text: We mapped a 10-minute drive area in Valhalla using the ordinary car profile and the published road network. The table compares three hospital street-address points. The run used standard travel costs and no traffic for a specific time of day. Use the hospital’s site map to locate the appropriate entrance when an access decision depends on the final destination.

sections.heading: How do you find the assigned public school for a property?

blocks.text: Johnson County’s district map places the three site reference points in Blue Valley USD 229. Its grade-specific layers show Mission Trail Elementary, Leawood Middle, and Blue Valley North High. The results agree across the sampled area. The district’s official locator asks for an exact home address. Use that lookup for each new dwelling and the year the household will enroll.

From the site reference point, the county’s Prairie Star Middle campus point is about 1.30 straight-line miles away. Leawood Middle is about 1.83 miles away. The attendance result is Leawood Middle. The point distances help compare proximity while the attendance layer answers the enrollment question.

sections.heading: How do you check the fire department and ambulance service?

blocks.text: The county Fire Service Area layer returned Leawood Fire at all three site points. Leawood’s standards of cover describe shared county dispatch, automatic aid, and Johnson County MED-ACT ambulance transport. Consult the current agency records when a project needs dispatch area, response history, or transport assumptions.

The property file also has a separate review of site access for emergency vehicles. The city’s Fire Marshal memo, dated April 13, 2026, says that previous comments on the preliminary plan had been resolved. Keep that memo with the version of the plan it reviewed. The county provider boundary and the city plan review support different parts of the property file.

faqs.question: How do I know which fire department serves an address?
faqs.answer: Look up the address in the county fire-service or emergency-response layer and confirm the result with the local authority. Read the agency’s coverage or dispatch documentation when you need details about how calls are handled.

faqs.question: Is the nearest school the one a home is assigned to?
faqs.answer: Check the school district’s address locator for the relevant grade and school year. A campus can be closer while falling outside the home’s attendance assignment.

faqs.question: How can a hospital show different emergency-service information in two public sources?
faqs.answer: Keep the general facility flag, other CMS measures, and the hospital’s current service listing as separate records. Join by CMS Certification Number and compare the periods and location. These sources differed at the Saint Luke’s South campus in the Leawood example.

faqs.question: Can a car drive-time map estimate ambulance response time?
faqs.answer: Ordinary car routing estimates travel over a street network. For ambulance response, use agency data on call handling, vehicle availability, dispatch and travel, and identify the period and area measured.

title: How to calculate retail trade area overlap
description: Measure the households two retail sites can both reach. Compare 10-, 15- and 20-minute drive times at two Detroit grocery stores, with downloadable Census estimates.
coverAlt: Aerial map with the two 15-minute Detroit drive areas and three zones. Micah’s only reaches about 247,700 households, both reach 31,200, and Whittier’s only reaches 150,300.
coverCaption: Estimated Michigan households by 15-minute drive area. Routes from Valhalla and © OpenStreetMap contributors, over USDA aerial imagery via USGS.
intro: To calculate retail trade area overlap, intersect the two store boundaries and count the households in the shared area. Then count the candidate’s households outside the existing store’s boundary. That second number estimates how much household reach the proposed store adds under the chosen travel-time assumptions.
takeaways: Create the two drive areas using the same travel mode, destination direction, time cutoff and traffic settings.
Count existing-only, shared and candidate-only households separately. When you total the two locations, count the shared households once.
Use the shared area to investigate possible sales transfer. Shopping behavior and sales forecasts need evidence from customers and comparable stores.

sections.heading: How do you calculate trade area overlap?

blocks.text: Start at the customer entrance or access point for each store, then model inbound drive times. Subtract each drive area from the other and keep the intersection as a third area. For a proposed store near several existing locations, first combine the existing drive areas into one boundary.

rows: Shared households
Count households in the intersection.
How many households can reach both locations under the model?
Additional household reach
Count households inside the candidate boundary and outside the existing boundary.
How much modeled reach would the candidate add?
Candidate overlap share
Divide shared households by all households in the candidate boundary.
How much of the candidate’s reachable market can already reach the existing store?
Total household reach
Count the union, or add the two store counts and subtract the shared count once.
How many distinct households can reach at least one store?

blocks.text: For households, use each 2020 Census block’s internal point to assign its housing units to an area. Calculate the share of each block group’s housing units in the area and apply that share to its ACS household estimate. Use the share of land and water area when a block group has no housing units in the base data. Household overlap and square-mile overlap answer different questions because people are unevenly distributed.

sections.heading: What changed between a 10- and 20-minute drive in Detroit?

blocks.text: We checked Micah’s Market and Whittier Bodega with the same Valhalla settings on November 24, 2026. The starting coordinates came from Census address-range matches. The runs modeled inbound travel and used no time-specific traffic inputs. The table uses 2020–2024 American Community Survey estimates allocated to the Michigan portions of each drive area.

columns: Share of Whittier’s area households also in Micah’s
rows: 10 minutes
0. The modeled polygons are disjoint.
15 minutes
20 minutes

blocks.text: At 15 minutes, the two catchments cover about 429,200 distinct Michigan households. Adding both store estimates would count the overlapping 31,200 twice. Using block-group area shares instead of 2020 housing units puts the shared estimate at about 34,000. The original shared estimate has an ACS sampling margin of about 1,000 households at 90% confidence. That margin leaves out uncertainty from the drive-time model and from how households are allocated within each block group.

sections.heading: Does overlapping reach predict sales cannibalization?

blocks.text: Shared drive-time households are candidates for further study. Estimate sales transfer using aggregated customer origins, comparable-store openings and the two locations’ assortments, prices and access. Account for nearby competitors and how much demand the new store could win from them. Test travel times at the hours customers are likely to shop.

Keep the store entrances, routing date, boundaries, denominator and demographic release the same when you compare sites. Ask a vendor to return the polygons and inputs as well as the count so your team can reproduce the result.
