faqs.question: Should I measure overlap by area or households?
faqs.answer: Use household overlap for a question about reachable residents. A square-mile share describes the geometry. An intersection can include water, industrial land or other areas with few households.

faqs.question: Why is the overlap percentage different depending on which store I start with?
faqs.answer: The two catchments share the same intersection. Dividing that shared count by the candidate’s total answers how much of the candidate’s market is shared. Dividing by the existing store’s total answers a different question.

faqs.question: Can walking and driving trade areas be compared?
faqs.answer: Keep the travel mode and cutoff visible on each result. For a walk-in format, calculate walking overlap separately. Use the modeled mode that best reflects how customers reach the site.

title: How to Calculate Drive-Time Demographics With Census Data
description: Estimate population, households, income and employment around a retail site. Compare a 10-minute drive with a three-mile radius at two Detroit grocery stores.
coverAlt: Aerial map of Detroit with drive, walking and radius boundaries for Micah’s Market and Whittier Bodega. The drive estimates are 236,500 and 140,200 residents, compared with 158,200 and 150,500 in the three-mile radius.
coverCaption: The 10-minute drive adds roughly 78,000 estimated residents at Micah’s Market and removes roughly 10,000 at Whittier Bodega compared with the three-mile radius.
intro: To calculate drive-time demographics, map the roads people can use to reach a site, then allocate Census estimates where the travel boundary cuts through a block group. We tested this at two Detroit grocery stores. The estimated population around Micah’s Market was 236,500 within a modeled 10-minute drive and 158,200 within a three-mile radius. At Whittier Bodega, the drive pulled in fewer residents than the radius did.
takeaways: Compare the same travel mode, direction, and cutoff at every candidate site. A fixed radius can overstate the reachable population in one trade area and understate it in another.
Keep the Census release, tract or block group identifiers, allocation weights, and sampling margins with the estimate.
Use resident counts to compare the opportunity around each site. Add competitor locations, physical access, visits, and local observations before committing to a store.

sections.heading: How does a 10-minute drive compare with a three-mile radius?

blocks.text: Micah’s Market at 15924 Fenkell Avenue and Whittier Bodega at 11009 Whittier Avenue opened through Detroit’s Green Grocer Program in 2026. We geocoded their public street addresses and drew a three-mile circle around each. We also mapped the areas from which people could reach each store within ten minutes by car or on foot. The table uses the same Census release for every boundary.

rows: Three-mile radius
10-minute drive to the store
10-minute walk to the store

blocks.text: The difference at Micah’s Market was about 78,300 more residents for the drive boundary. At Whittier Bodega the drive reached about 10,300 fewer. The gap between stores was about 96,300 residents for the drive and 7,700 for the circle. In the 10-minute walk comparison, the difference was about 600 residents and the sampling margin on that difference was about 1,150. The walk results provide less basis to prefer one location by population alone.

The intervals in the table show ACS sampling uncertainty after holding the map and weighting method fixed. Travel speeds, street crossings, the actual store entrance, and the distribution of homes within a block group can shift the estimates independently of that margin.

blocks.text: Household income here is the share below $50,000 in 2024 dollars. We summed the published income bands, divided by total households, and repeated that calculation across the Census variance replicates. To estimate a catchment median, use income distribution bins and disclose the interpolation method. An average of block-group medians can give a different answer.

The three-mile circle showed more employed residents near Whittier Bodega, about 59,600 versus 54,500. The drive boundary reversed that comparison, with about 82,600 near Micah’s Market and 56,100 near Whittier Bodega. These are civilian employed residents aged 16 and over. For jobs located near the store or daytime activity, use a workplace-based source such as Census OnTheMap and retain its geography and year.

sections.heading: How do you join Census data to a drive-time polygon?

blocks.text: Begin with the entrance people will use. In this study the inputs were Census geocodes interpolated along street segments, and the routes were snapped to nearby network edges. Valhalla modeled inbound car and pedestrian trips over OpenStreetMap. Save the coordinates, mode, direction, cutoff, network date and returned polygon. The study used standard travel costs without traffic for a specific time of day.

Intersect the boundary with the block groups for the ACS release. For a partially covered group, count the share of its 2020 Census block population whose internal points fall inside the boundary. Apply that share to its ACS counts of residents and employed residents. For household counts and income bands, use the share of 2020 housing units. An intersected area fraction fills in when a block group has no 2020 population or housing base for that weight.

Apply the same weights to each of the 80 ACS survey replicates. To compare two catchments, subtract their estimates within each matched replicate before calculating the sampling margin on the difference. We also reran the counts using only the share of each block group’s area inside the polygon. At Micah’s Market the drive estimate rose by about 4,400 residents under that alternative. The difference shows how the allocation assumption can matter even when the road boundary stays fixed.

Ask for the input geometry, travel settings, data release and treatment of partial areas. Compare with one catchment you can reconstruct.
Calculate and retain the street-network boundary
Valhalla can model travel toward a destination. Mapbox Isochrone provides published driving, traffic, walking and cycling profiles.

blocks.text: For a grocery operator, the first useful comparison is often walkable households and the locations of nearby stores with similar offerings. A medical practice may start with catchment population and age bands, then add competing providers and actual travel at appointment times. A landlord comparing tenants can apply the same methods to separate residents, daytime employment, and measured visits. Keep a version of the inputs so changes in population can be distinguished from changes in the routing network.

faqs.question: Can I get Census demographics for a 10-minute drive from an address?
faqs.answer: Yes. Generate the travel-time polygon, intersect it with the Census geography for the selected release, and allocate estimates for partial block groups. Save the polygon and weighting method so someone can reproduce the result.

faqs.question: What is the difference between a radius and a drive-time trade area?
faqs.answer: A radius includes everything inside a straight-line distance. A drive-time area follows allowed routes, turns, and estimated travel costs. A radius is handy for a quick check. Before comparing retail sites, test whether the road-based boundary changes the answer.

faqs.question: Does the Census sampling margin include routing or mapping errors?
faqs.answer: No. It describes sampling uncertainty for the estimate under the chosen settings. A changed entrance, congestion, or different allocation of households within block groups can shift the estimate independently.

faqs.question: Does a drive-time population estimate tell me how many customers I will get?
faqs.answer: It estimates residents associated with the modeled area. To estimate store demand, add competing businesses, the store’s offer and hours, site access and evidence of actual visits or spending.

title: How to Use Geologic Maps and Well Logs for Site Due Diligence
description: Find geologic maps, water well logs, and geotechnical reports for industrial land. See which records answer questions about soils, bedrock, and groundwater.
coverAlt: Aerial map of a Stayton industrial tax lot in geologic unit Qg1. The chart shows on-site augers at 2–3 feet, water first found at 35 feet and a 5-foot static level in one nearby well, and a separate 15-foot static level in the other.
coverCaption: The water levels apply to two nearby wells. The five site borings were dry to their termination depths of 2 to 3 feet.
intro: Start with the parcel boundary, then pull the original geologic map, nearby well logs, and any geotechnical reports filed for the site. Each record answers a different question. At an industrial parcel in Stayton, Oregon, the regional map showed sand and gravel. One nearby well recorded water first found at 35 feet and a static water level of 5 feet, while five on-site hand augers reached only 2 to 3 feet.
takeaways: Use the original map scale and publication date to judge how much detail a parcel overlay supports.
Keep water first encountered, static water level, and total drilled depth in separate fields.
Ask for fieldwork at the proposed building pads, trenches, or basins before relying on a site groundwater or bedrock depth.

sections.heading: Where can I find geology and groundwater records for a property?

blocks.text: Start with the county tax lot or a survey boundary for the land you are evaluating. The USGS National Geologic Map Database and state geological surveys index source maps. State well report searches hold drillers’ construction records, and county or city development files may contain geotechnical reports, grading plans, or drainage studies for the same property.

rows: What material does the regional map show?
The state geology layer and the original map cited for that polygon.
Unit name, polygon or map identifier, original scale, and date.
How deep was water in nearby wells?
Original well logs and, where available, dated monitoring readings.
Well identifier, location precision, date, measurement reference, static level, and water-bearing intervals.
What did someone actually find on this property?
Boring logs and test locations in a project geotechnical report.
The tested locations and depths, refusal, groundwater observations, and how the investigation relates to the proposed work.

sections.heading: What did the geologic map show for the Stayton parcel?

blocks.text: We joined Marion County tax lot 091W09DA01103 at 1319 W Washington Street to Oregon’s geologic compilation. The entire county polygon fell within Qg1, the map unit for sand and gravel deposited after the Missoula Floods. Oregon’s 2025 compilation traces this polygon to a 2001 USGS map at 1:250,000 scale. The overlap establishes what that map assigns to the property. Bedrock depth and the thickness of individual layers still require site evidence.

sections.heading: What is the difference between static water level and water first found?

blocks.text: A driller records the first water encounter as a depth during drilling. The static level records where water stands in the well under non-pumping conditions at the time of measurement. Those readings can be very different, even in the same well. Record the measurement date and the reference used for each depth before comparing nearby wells.

rows: MARI 13574
5 feet on May 3, 1979
35 feet
39 feet
MARI 13572
15 feet on May 8, 1965
No separate depth recorded on the form
40 feet

blocks.text: A later groundwater addendum describes two wells within half a mile and gives water encounter depths of 35 and 40 feet. The first scan confirms 35 feet in the encounter field. The second records 40 feet as both drilled and completed depth. The download preserves the addendum’s statement and leaves the second log’s encounter depth blank. The published drainage report separately cites a range of 5 to 15 feet for static water levels in the nearby wells.

sections.heading: What could the on-site borings tell a buyer?

blocks.text: The 2021 geotechnical report logged five hand augers on April 12. Three reached 2 feet and two reached 3 feet. Four logs report refusal, meaning the auger could not advance using that method. The report describes gravel and abundant river rocks in the tested materials. None of those shallow holes encountered groundwater.

The two deeper augers supported infiltration testing for the proposed basins. A buyer considering an excavation below the explored depth should ask the project engineer what additional borings and groundwater observations the new design requires. Give the engineer the proposed pad elevations, trench and basin locations, finished excavation depths, and schedule so the investigation can address the actual work.

sections.heading: How should a buyer screen for karst, subsidence, or old mines?

rows: Karst and sinkholes
State geology, any published karst or sinkhole inventory, and terrain depressions.
Have a qualified practitioner review the rock type, drainage, and planned structures to determine what investigation is warranted.
Gradual subsidence
Published measurements of land motion and agency reports on the cause and dates.
Check whether the measurement period and spatial coverage capture the proposed footprint. Ask about settlement tolerances for the structures and utilities.
Historical mine workings
State mine inventory and original workings maps where available.
Request map location, underground extent, and records of treatment or reclamation. A documented mine entrance may be outside the area above its workings.

blocks.text: Use these as separate screening questions. The Stayton example evaluates records of surface geology and groundwater. Comparable diligence for a lender, underwriter, or acquisition team can turn each issue into a document request tied to the property and proposed work.

sections.heading: Which Invariant Earth API fields help screen land at scale?

blocks.text: Invariant Earth’s public field catalog includes USDA general soil-map depth to bedrock, the shallowest restrictive layer in the dominant detailed soil-map component, and the latest published depth to water for the nearest eligible USGS monitoring location within 15 kilometers. The bedrock field may be a lower bound. The monitoring reading can be historical and applies to the monitoring location. Keep notes, dates, and missing values with the result when you compare parcels.

Use these fields to prioritize which parcels need a state map, original well report, or site investigation. Store the original records under the same parcel identifier so the next reviewer can see exactly what changed and which findings came from fieldwork.

faqs.question: Can a nearby well show the groundwater depth on my parcel?
faqs.answer: A nearby well can show what was measured in that well on a given date. Water level on the proposed site depends on local conditions, elevations and season. Use nearby logs to inform the field investigation and compare measurements against the design elevations.

faqs.question: Does auger refusal mean the crew reached bedrock?
faqs.answer: Refusal means the tool could no longer advance under the field method used. Read the materials and termination notes before interpreting the refusal. At Stayton the shallow field logs describe gravel and river rocks.

faqs.question: Can I use a geologic map to estimate depth to bedrock?
faqs.answer: Use the map to identify the mapped surface or near-surface unit and its publication scale. Request subsurface records or targeted investigation when excavation or foundation decisions depend on the elevation of bedrock.

title: How to Check Power Outage and Road Closure History
description: Find historical outages and road closures near a facility. Compare county readings, state snapshots, and I-40 reopening records from Hurricane Helene.
coverAlt: Graph of public Haywood County outage observations with a peak of 23,076 on September 27, 2024, next to a 2022 aerial of the Pigeon River Gorge. I-40 reopened with one lane each way on March 1, 2025.
coverCaption: The power observations are for Haywood County. The road reopening applies to the I-40 gorge segment. The 2022 USDA aerial shows the terrain before Helene.
intro: To check disruption history near a facility, match local outage records to the service address and road reports to the routes people and freight actually use. County and state outage data help identify periods to investigate. After Hurricane Helene, Haywood County’s highest observed outage count was 23,076 customers on September 27, 2024. The damaged stretch of I-40 in the Pigeon River Gorge reopened with one lane in each direction on March 1, 2025.
takeaways: Use county data to identify when to request exact service interruptions from the utility or facility operator.
Save the observation time, reporting geography, and source. Keep missing measurements separate from reported zeros.
Check reopening restrictions for the vehicles a facility needs. An open road can still have lane limits, detours or size restrictions.

sections.heading: Where can I find outage and road closure history for a location?

rows: Did this facility lose utility service?
Serving utility’s service interruption record for the premise or meter, plus facility power logs.
A service-level timeline. Compare with generator or transfer-switch logs to see whether the site itself lost power.
When did the surrounding area have outages?
ORNL EAGLE-I county observations, DOE situation reports, or DOE-417 incident summaries.
Observed customer counts by reporting geography or incidents that meet the applicable reporting criteria.
Could employees or trucks reach the site?
State or local DOT incident records and notices for the route, direction, entry point and vehicle class.
Reported closure, detour, reopening and restrictions for a specific road segment.

blocks.text: For a facility, use the service address and serving utility to request premise-level records. For road access, trace the primary and backup routes from the actual site entrance. Check the direction of travel and whether the detour is usable by the trucks or other vehicles the site relies on.

sections.heading: How did reported power outages change after Helene?

blocks.text: EAGLE-I recorded its highest Haywood County count in the study window at 6:15 p.m. Eastern Daylight Time on September 27, 2024. The count was 23,076 customers. The window ran from September 25 through October 15 in local time. EAGLE-I provided values for 1,996 of the 2,016 quarter-hour slots. The download preserves all 20 missing observations and the one reported zero.

The Department of Energy published separate statewide snapshots. We joined them to county values only when the recorded timestamps matched exactly. The resulting table shows counts from each source at the same time, with each source’s geographic scope intact.

rows: September 27, 3:00 p.m.
October 2, 3:00 p.m.
October 9, 10:00 a.m.
October 11, 10:00 a.m.
October 15, 12:30 p.m.

blocks.text: The statewide snapshots kept falling between October 9 and 11 while the county readings at those times rose. The county series is based on utility public outage maps. It can include later interruptions or changes in reporting. The two counts alone cannot establish which customers lost or regained power, or why.

blocks.label: Download the county time series, 15 state snapshots, and I-40 closure milestones

sections.heading: When did I-40 reopen in the Pigeon River Gorge?

blocks.text: NCDOT reported severe damage on September 27, 2024, and said it closed the interstate immediately. Traffic resumed March 1, 2025, a difference of 155 calendar days. NCDOT described a temporary pattern with one lane each way for about 12 miles between North Carolina Exit 7 and Tennessee Exit 447.

rows: September 27, 2024
Helene damage prompted closure.
Through traffic stopped on the affected segment.
December 20, 2024
NCDOT reported additional roadway damage.
The agency delayed its planned temporary reopening.
March 1, 2025
The temporary lanes opened.
One lane each way. North Carolina’s reopening guidance allowed standard 18-wheelers and excluded wide loads.
A separate rockslide closed the gorge segment again.
The interval between closure and reopening dates was nine calendar days.

blocks.text: For freight diligence, record the restrictions in effect at each reopening. NCDOT’s March guidance described a 35 mph limit on the North Carolina side and warned standard 18-wheelers against suggested local alternates beyond Exit 20. A historical opening date cannot answer whether the route is open today. For current conditions, check the relevant DOT traffic service.

sections.heading: What should an outage and road closure API return for a site?

blocks.text: Keep separate time fields for when an incident happened, when a count was observed, and when a source published or updated the record. Identify the geography and unit for power counts. Store the road segment and direction with closure state, restriction details, and whether an opening was scheduled or confirmed. Preserve gaps in coverage.

Invariant Earth’s public field catalog documents nearby road names, classes and distances. Those fields can help identify candidate approaches before you check the official road event records for each route. When you assess resilience, keep documented service interruptions, utility-wide reliability statistics, and access interruptions attached to the right geography.

items.label: Compare annual freight volumes before checking route disruptions

faqs.question: Can I find historical power outages by address?
faqs.answer: Ask the serving utility for records associated with the service premise or meter, subject to the utility’s access rules. County and state data show surrounding conditions. Facility logs can establish how the site’s equipment and backup systems responded.

faqs.question: Does a missing outage record mean the power was on?
faqs.answer: A missing observation leaves the customer count unknown. Keep missing values separate from a measured zero and use utility or facility records for conclusions about an individual site.

faqs.question: How do I find past road closures near a property?
faqs.answer: Use the DOT incident or public notice archive for the road, direction and segment. Save the closure date, the confirmed reopening, restrictions, and links to the notices. Check the current feed separately for travel planning.

title: How to Find Farmland Crop History by Parcel
description: Use USDA crop maps to check five years of crop cover, verify narrow-field errors against Iowa State’s farm records, and compare soils and irrigation evidence.
coverAlt: Side by side maps compare Iowa State’s 2020 crop records with the USDA 30-metre crop map. The map’s dominant class matches 13 of 35 research plots with consistent reference records.
coverCaption: Both maps show the same research plots. The farm records and crop classes describe 2020. The contextual aerial image is USDA NAIP 2023.
intro: Start with the field boundary and clip each year of the USDA Cropland Data Layer to it. Record the area assigned to each crop, the raster resolution and which years have field records for comparison. At Iowa State’s Marsden Farm, the USDA map’s dominant class matched the 2020 crop records on 13 of 35 research plots with consistent records. The plots are about 18 metres wide, narrower than the 30-metre crop pixels used that year.
takeaways: Keep crop class and mapped acreage for each year. An overall dominant crop can hide a rotation and combine distinct fields on one parcel.
Compare classification to grower or research records where field edges, narrow strips or cover crops affect an important decision.
Review soils, drainage, water use and irrigation authorization separately before valuing a property or underwriting production.

sections.heading: Where can I find the last five years of crop history for a property?

blocks.text: USDA NASS publishes annual crop classes through CroplandCROS and its national Cropland Data Layer downloads. Start with the growing area for the field in question, retaining the assessor parcel separately when it also contains a farmstead, roads or neighboring fields. Use an equal-area projection to clip the raster and report the acreage for each class, including uncultivated classes and any missing coverage.

The examples below use the same 13.64-acre footprint of 36 Marsden research plots. We excluded the access and separation strips identified in the plot layout. We requested USDA’s categorical data on a 30-metre grid for 2021 through 2023 and a 10-metre grid for 2024 and 2025, following the original products’ nominal resolutions. The finer grid and changes in how USDA generated the classes can affect comparisons across those years.

blocks.text: The table shows three mapped classes. The download includes every class that intersects the plots, including 1.13 acres mapped as oats and 0.89 as alfalfa in 2025. The 2021 through 2025 rows describe USDA classifications over the historical plot footprint. Two farm reference records were available to cross-check the 2020 map.

blocks.label: Download the annual crop grids, plot comparisons, and soil map units

sections.heading: Can a crop map recover a field’s actual rotation?

blocks.text: Iowa State tested two-, three-, and four-year rotations at Marsden Farm. The rotations combine corn and soybeans with oats and companion forage in the longer systems. We matched the numbered plot geometries to the farm’s 2020 layout and crop key. One plot was excluded because the layout labels plot 33 as soybeans and the crop key labels it as the oat phase.

Of the 35 plots where the two farm records agree, the crop class covering the most area matched on 13. Sampling only the centre pixel matched on 12. For example, the farm records list soybeans on plot 43, where the USDA map classified about 88% of the plot as corn. The map’s smallest unit was wider than a typical plot, and the rotations included crops grown together. Treat these results as a check on the narrow Marsden research plots.

When crop sequence affects a purchase or lease, ask for dated planting and harvest records tied to the same field boundaries. Keep the mapped class shares with the field-level reference and compare each year separately. An acreage-weighted dominant crop is useful for screening, while annual records preserve the alternation of crops.

sections.heading: How do I check soil productivity for the same field?

blocks.text: Intersect the same field boundary with the USDA NRCS soil map units. For Iowa’s Corn Suitability Rating 2, or CSR2, multiply each current rating by the acres of overlap, add those products, and divide by the acreage with ratings. Save the rating source and the soil survey version with the calculation.

Our 13.64-acre footprint intersected six Boone County soil map units and had an area-weighted CSR2 of 87.3. About 5.78 acres fell in units classified as prime farmland if drained. The rating describes relative corn-growing potential under the rating assumptions. For valuation, check drainage condition and historical yields separately.

sections.heading: How do I verify whether farmland is irrigated?

blocks.text: The 2022 Census of Agriculture reports 561 irrigated acres and 563 acres with irrigation systems or equipment present for Boone County. Those are two different county measures. Neither identifies the irrigated fields or proves what water is available to the research plots.

For a specific Iowa property, check the Department of Natural Resources water-use permit registry and get the underlying permit, any amendments and the annual water-use reports. Match the permit holder, withdrawal location, authorized amount, reporting period and the land actually served. Confirm the current equipment and recorded use with the operator.

sections.heading: What should a parcel crop history API return?

blocks.text: Invariant Earth’s field catalog documents a five-year dominant crop at a 30-metre cell, with the annual history in the field notes, and SSURGO point fields for soil map unit and drainage class. For acreage or underwriting, request the field or parcel boundary and keep the annual grids or class shares with crop year, resolution and the calculation method. Report field records and any permit or usage evidence under their own sources.

items.label: Check crop, soil and drought fields in the Earth API

faqs.question: How do I look up what was grown on a parcel?
faqs.answer: Use the field boundary and the USDA Cropland Data Layer for each growing season. Clip each year to the same boundary, retain the mapped acreage by crop class, and check important years against planting or harvest records.

faqs.question: Does USDA crop data show a corn-soybean rotation?
faqs.answer: Annual corn and soybean classes can indicate a rotation. Look at the sequence for each field over several years and keep both classes where the map shows them. A single dominant crop across years obscures the sequence.

faqs.question: Is Corn Suitability Rating 2 a yield estimate?
faqs.answer: CSR2 is a relative rating for Iowa soil map units. Calculate an area-weighted rating for a tract and use actual field yield histories separately when estimating production.

title: How to Calculate Parcel Slope and Screen Developable Land
description: Compare a 3-foot lidar grid with a 30-foot average and USGS 3DEP. See how resolution changes acres under a slope cutoff and download the source data.
coverAlt: The same 19.74-acre parcel on 2022 aerial imagery. A 3-foot lidar grid shows 16.28 acres at or below 5% slope. Averaging the same elevations to a 30-foot grid shows 19.74 acres at or below 5%.
coverCaption: One elevation source and the same parcel and cutoff in both panels. Orange cells exceed 5% on the native grid. Aerial imagery is from USDA NAIP.
intro: To calculate how much land meets a slope cutoff, derive slope from a bare-earth elevation model and measure the qualifying area inside the parcel. Save the resolution, acquisition dates, cutoff, and largest adjoining area. On a 19.74-acre Oregon parcel, 16.28 acres met an illustrative 5% cutoff on a 3-foot lidar grid. Averaging the same source onto a 30-foot grid increased that estimate to 19.74 acres.
takeaways: Use lidar-derived bare-earth elevation for slope. Keep dated aerial imagery alongside it to review roads, cover, and visible changes.
Calculate slope on elevation data that extend beyond the parcel, then clip the result. Measure the actual overlap of cells along the boundary.
Report the combined qualifying acreage and the largest adjoining area. Carry the elevation source and uncertainty into any layout or grading review.

sections.heading: How much can elevation resolution change a slope estimate?

blocks.text: The study uses the current Marion County polygon for tax lot 091W04B001000 near Stayton. Oregon’s DOGAMI Stayton quadrangle includes a 3-foot bare-earth grid from the 2008–2009 Willamette Valley acquisition. We averaged complete 10-by-10 blocks from that grid to create the 30-foot comparison, then calculated slope on both. This tests what happened when we changed the grid size while using the same original elevations.

rows: 2% or less
10.77 acres
16.48 acres
16.18 acres
5% or less
16.28 acres
19.74 acres

10% or less

blocks.text: At 5%, the total estimate grew by 3.46 acres after averaging the fine grid. The largest group of qualifying cells that share an edge grew from 13.05 to 19.74 acres. For a buyer trying to fit a 15-acre footprint, the fine grid would prompt a closer review of where flatter ground adjoins. The raster figures describe slope alone. Utilities, access, drainage, wetlands and layout still matter.

The USGS product is a separately published elevation grid. Its cells measured about 7.32 metres east to west and 10.29 metres north to south at this site. The 19.65-acre result at 5% is useful for an initial screen. Changes in source, processing or grid alignment can also affect comparisons between the USGS and Oregon products.

blocks.label: Download both elevation windows, the parcel boundary, and the slope results

sections.heading: How do I calculate slope percentage and acreage from a DEM?

blocks.text: Download a bare-earth digital elevation model, or DEM, for the parcel and surrounding ground. Use the full buffered grid to estimate slope and apply the boundary afterward. Horn’s method uses a 3-by-3 group of cells, so clipping elevation first can leave gaps or alter the estimate around the edge.

Slope in percent is 100 times the rise divided by the horizontal run. For a raster, estimate the gradients east to west and north to south and combine their magnitude. Match horizontal distance and elevation units. On a latitude and longitude grid, measure the east-to-west and north-to-south cell spacing in metres at the site. A 5% grade is about 2.86 degrees.

Clip eligible cells to the parcel and sum the area of the intersections in an equal-area projection. Use a proportional weight for cells crossed by the lot boundary. Check that the clipped cells cover the entire lot and report any missing elevation coverage. For one connected-area estimate, count cells that share an edge and report the largest group by acreage.

sections.heading: How should I compare lidar and aerial imagery dates?

blocks.text: The Oregon lidar delivery used for this lot lists a 2008–2009 acquisition range, NAVD88 elevations in international feet and the Geoid03 model. The USGS tile has a 2025 publication date and NAVD88 elevations in metres. A tile publication date can be newer than the underlying surveys. Check acquisition, vertical datum, units and surface type before comparing elevations across sources.

The 2020 and 2022 USDA aerials use the same mapped footprint. The central field looks greener and the field tracks are more distinct in the 2020 image. Treat those as visual observations and check acquisition conditions before interpreting them. Use comparable elevation surveys to investigate a change in ground height.

items.label: Review the wetland inventory, soil map and agency determination for this parcel

sections.heading: What should a slope data API return for site selection?

blocks.text: Invariant Earth’s public field catalog documents point elevation and point slope, including how the 3DEP tile supports the slope calculation. For a parcel-wide screen, keep the boundary identifier, elevation product, capture and publication dates where available, grid spacing, slope units and cutoff. Return total qualifying acreage and the largest adjoining area with the calculation method.

Align the slope cutoff with the intended building, yard, road or solar layout. Have the design team check candidate areas against a current survey, grading plan and the project’s drainage and geotechnical requirements.

faqs.question: How do I find slope data for a property?
faqs.answer: Retrieve the parcel boundary and look up bare-earth elevation in the USGS National Map or the state lidar archive. Record the grid resolution and source date, calculate slope on a buffered window, then measure the results inside the parcel.

faqs.question: Can USGS 10-metre terrain data show whether an entire parcel is flat?
faqs.answer: It can support a regional screen. Check finer lidar where service roads, banks or small drainage features could affect the layout. In the Stayton test, 19.65 acres met a 5% cutoff on the USGS grid and 16.28 acres met it on the native 3-foot grid.

faqs.question: What is the difference between slope in degrees and percent grade?
faqs.answer: Percent grade is 100 times the tangent of the slope angle. A slope of 5 degrees is about 8.75% grade. A 5% grade is about 2.86 degrees.

title: How to Check a Property for Wetlands and Hydric Soils
description: Use wetlands maps, hydric soils, and a Corps determination to screen land for development. Download the parcel and soil data from a real Oregon case.
coverAlt: Aerial map of tax lot 1000 near Stayton, Oregon. The 19.74-acre lot has zero mapped National Wetlands Inventory acres and overlaps a hydric soil map unit by 1.76 acres. A separate Corps record describes Wetland 4 as 1.87 acres.
coverCaption: The county lot is outlined in cream, the hydric soil map unit is shaded gold within the lot, and the National Wetlands Inventory is in blue. Sources include USDA NAIP 2022 aerial imagery, Marion County GIS, USFWS, NRCS, and the Corps.
intro: Start with the current parcel boundary and the area the project would disturb, including access and utility routes. Overlay the National Wetlands Inventory, local wetland inventories, and USDA soil polygons. Then check for a field delineation and federal or state decisions that cover the work area. On a 19.74-acre lot near Stayton, Oregon, the federal inventory had zero overlap. A USDA map unit with hydric soil components covered 1.76 acres of the lot, and a Corps record separately described a 1.87-acre wetland on the east side.
takeaways: Clip inventory and soil polygons to the parcel or proposed disturbance boundary before reporting acreage. Keep each layer’s dates and scope with the result.
Hydric soil components flag places to investigate. A map unit’s representative component percentages cannot locate individual soils or delineate a wetland.
Check the field delineation and the agency review boundary before using an acreage figure in a layout, closing condition, or permit estimate.

sections.heading: Which maps and records should I check before developing land?

rows: County parcel and site plan
Current tax lot, survey boundary, grading, access and utility corridors
Set the desktop screening footprint. Use a survey or legal description to resolve boundary disputes.
National Wetlands Inventory and state or local inventories
Mapped wetland and water polygons, mapping date and coverage
Identify mapped features in and near the work area, including the approaches to crossings.
USDA SSURGO soil survey
Soil map unit, hydric ratings of its components and survey version
Identify soil map units that warrant field checks. Keep the lot overlap and representative component percentages as separate attributes.
Field delineation and agency decisions
Delineated feature boundaries, source dates, agency review area and feature findings
Work with the relevant agencies to determine which approvals the proposed grading, fill and crossings require.

blocks.text: For acreage, use a suitable equal-area projection, clip the layers to the review boundary, and dissolve overlaps within each layer. Keep mapped wetland acres, soil map-unit acres, and independently verified field acres in separate columns. A wetland polygon’s full acreage can include land outside your property.

sections.heading: What did the maps miss on the Stayton property?

blocks.text: The current Marion County boundary for lot 091W04B001000, abbreviated 091W04B01000 on the Corps map, measures 19.74 acres in our equal-area GIS calculation. We checked that polygon against the National Wetlands Inventory and SSURGO on November 23, 2026. The Corps made its determination for a separate 60.9-acre review area that included portions of multiple tax lots.

rows: National Wetlands Inventory
0.00 acres
No inventory polygon intersected the current county lot in the downloaded layer.
USDA soil map unit 2224A
1.76 acres
Parcel overlap with Courtney gravelly silty clay loam, about 8.94% of the lot. The NRCS component list includes hydric soils.
Corps Wetland 4
1.87 acres
Published feature size in the January 2026 determination. The Corps locates it on the east side of lot 1000 and says it continues east beyond the agency review area.

blocks.text: The soil map unit’s four listed components are rated hydric and total 97% by representative component percentage. SSURGO provides the boundary of the map unit. A field crew still has to locate soil conditions and any wetland edge within it. Our download includes the county geometry, the nearby inventory polygons, the clipped soil map units, and the separate Corps findings.

blocks.label: Download parcel and soil geometries, source queries, and Corps findings

sections.heading: What does an approved jurisdictional determination tell a buyer?

blocks.text: The Corps’ January 12, 2026 determination NWP-2025-00423 describes four wetlands totaling 8.72 acres by the individual sizes it reports. It classifies Wetlands 3 and 4, totaling 3.91 acres, as jurisdictional under Section 404. It classifies Wetlands 1 and 2, totaling 4.81 acres, as non-jurisdictional in that determination. The Corps says Wetlands 3 and 4 abut Ditch 1, which it also determined to be jurisdictional.

The Corps wrote that it did not find Ditch 1 in either the National Wetlands Inventory or the National Hydrography Dataset consulted for the review. The memo gives its length as 2,359 linear feet. The map’s red Corps annotation gives 2,395 linear feet. Use the same jurisdiction finding in the record, then reconcile the governing geometry and length before estimating crossing impacts or mitigation quantities.

Check Oregon’s state process separately for work near wetlands and waters. The Department of State Lands describes its own determination, delineation review, and removal-fill permit process. The federal memo gives federal findings for the stated review area. The project’s grading and crossings, along with applicable state and local requirements, determine the next review steps.

sections.heading: How should a wetlands data API handle parcel screening?

blocks.text: Invariant Earth’s field catalog documents point-level checks for whether the point intersects an NWI polygon, distance to the nearest mapped wetland within 500 metres, and the SSURGO soil map-unit name and dominant-component drainage class. For parcel acreage, use the parcel and source polygons and calculate the intersection. The catalog’s wetland acreage represents the full selected inventory polygon.

In a GIS export or API response, retain the asset ID, boundary source, retrieval date, layer vintage where available, acres of intersection, and whether the provider returned data for the entire work area. Record the field delineation and any agency decision under their own identifiers. Use the result to decide where to commission fieldwork, check access or utilities, or revise the grading plan before pricing the site.

faqs.question: How do I find out if my land has wetlands?
faqs.answer: Check the National Wetlands Inventory and state or local wetland maps against the parcel and work area. Review soil and site conditions, then ask the appropriate agency or qualified consultant about a field delineation if the project could affect wetlands or waters.

faqs.question: Does a blank National Wetlands Inventory map mean the site is clear?
faqs.answer: A blank map or zero intersection means the particular inventory has no mapped polygon at that location. Inventory methods can miss resources. Site conditions, field delineation, and any applicable agency decisions still matter for development.

faqs.question: How do I calculate acres of mapped wetlands on a parcel?
faqs.answer: Retrieve the parcel and inventory polygons, project both to a suitable equal-area coordinate system, dissolve duplicate or overlapping inventory polygons, and measure the intersection with the parcel. Save the input vintages and the analysis boundary.

title: Census Tract Housing Vacancy and Rent Burden Data
description: Find Census tract vacancy and rent burden in ACS tables B25002 and B25070. Compare changing boundaries and calculate margins of error with a worked Austin example.
coverAlt: Two maps of the same part of Travis County. Tract 11 in the first map is split into tracts 11.01, 11.02 and 11.03 in the second. Estimated vacancy falls from 19.65% to 9.93% on the combined footprint.
coverCaption: The two maps use the same scale and footprint. Census TIGER/Line boundaries and American Community Survey table B25002.
intro: Use American Community Survey table B25002 for total and vacant housing units and table B25070 for the share of renter households spending at least 30% of their income on gross rent. To compare two periods, put both estimates on the same tract footprint and carry the survey’s uncertainty through the calculation. In an Austin-area example, the estimated share of housing units that were vacant fell from 19.65% to 9.93%. The evidence was too imprecise to tell whether rent burden rose or fell.
takeaways: Join ACS estimates to the tract identifiers and boundaries for their release year. Use the Census relationship file to match older and newer tract footprints.
Add the underlying counts before calculating a rate. Use the same calculation for each of the Census Bureau’s 80 variance replicates to estimate uncertainty.
For a planning memo or market comparison, report the survey period, denominator, geographic footprint and margin of error alongside each estimate.

sections.heading: Where can I download Census tract vacancy and rent burden data?

rows: Share of housing units vacant
B25002, line 003 divided by line 001
The share of all housing units classified as vacant, including seasonal units and other vacancies.
Share of renters spending at least 30% of income on gross rent
B25070, sum lines 007 through 010. Divide by line 001 minus line 011.
The share of renter-occupied housing units for which the gross-rent-to-income ratio can be computed and reaches the cutoff.

blocks.text: Use the five-year detailed tables at summary level 140 for tract estimates. The detailed-table downloads supply published counts and margins of error. The variance replicate archives include the additional values needed to calculate margins for derived rates and groups of tracts. Keep the 11-digit GEOID as text so a leading zero survives the join.

sections.heading: How do I compare housing data after a census tract splits?

blocks.text: Check the tract vintages before you match identifiers. The 2015–2019 ACS uses 2010 Census tracts, and the 2020–2024 ACS uses 2020 Census tracts with selected updates. The Census relationship file lists how older and newer tracts overlap, with separate land and water areas.

Old Tract 11 in Travis County, Texas (48453001100) split into tracts 11.01, 11.02 and 11.03. The Census relationship file assigns all 2,437,645 m² of land and 239,536 m² of water in the old tract to those three and shows that each successor sits wholly within the old footprint. Add the three 2020–2024 counts before you calculate the newer rates.

For a partial overlap, build a common geography from available finer-area counts or use a documented allocation method suited to the measure. The crosswalk gives an area of overlap. An area share alone cannot tell you what fraction of residents or housing units lived in that overlap.

sections.heading: What changed in Travis County’s former Tract 11?

blocks.text: The combined area had an estimated 5,715 housing units in 2015–2019 and 7,172 in 2020–2024. Estimated vacancies fell from 1,123 to 712 while housing stock grew. The change in the vacancy share excludes zero at the 90% confidence level. The change in the count of vacant units is less certain.

rows: Total housing units
Vacant housing units
Share of all housing units vacant
−9.72 ± 7.34 percentage points
Share of renters spending at least 30% of income on gross rent
−1.63 ± 11.11 percentage points

blocks.text: For rent burden, the estimated counts were 950 of 2,944 eligible renter households in the earlier period and 1,175 of 3,835 in the later period. The change in the share has an approximate 90% interval from a decline of 12.74 percentage points to an increase of 9.48 points. A planner can document the estimated rise in housing stock and lower vacancy share while recording the rent burden trend as indeterminate.

blocks.label: Download the tract crosswalk, Census estimates, 80 replicates and calculated results

sections.heading: How do I calculate the margin of error for a combined tract?

blocks.text: For each period, calculate the result from the published counts. Repeat the entire calculation for each of the 80 Census variance replicates, including the sums and division. Subtract the published-count result from each replicate result, square the differences, sum them and multiply by 4/80. The square root is the standard error. Multiply it by 1.645 for the 90% margin of error.

For a change between nonoverlapping periods, take the square root of the sum of the two squared margins. This gives an approximate 90% margin for the difference. If the resulting interval includes zero, report that the survey cannot establish a direction for the change. For near-zero or fully saturated rates, and for replicate denominators of zero, consult the Census Bureau’s special-case guidance.

sections.heading: What belongs in a housing data API response?

blocks.text: For address-based analysis, Invariant Earth’s field catalog documents a tract identifier and tract-level fields for occupied units, median home value and owner occupancy. Keep the vintage shown for each field with the response. For this historical comparison, join the two ACS releases and the Census geographic crosswalk, then store the numerator, denominator, margin and original source version with each derived rate.

Housing planners can use the comparison to decide which neighborhoods need a closer look. Developers and market analysts can use it alongside dated leasing data when evaluating current supply. For a measure of units available for rent, check vacancy status in B25004 and the date of any listing or inventory feed.

faqs.question: How do I get housing vacancy by census tract?
faqs.answer: Download ACS five-year detailed table B25002 at tract level. Divide vacant units on line 003 by total housing units on line 001. Retain the survey period and calculate the margin for the ratio.

faqs.question: Which Census table measures rent burden?
faqs.answer: In ACS table B25070, add the four categories starting at 30.0% of gross rent as a share of household income. Divide by the total renter-occupied units in the table after excluding the Not computed category.

faqs.question: Is the ACS share of vacant housing the same as the rental vacancy rate?
faqs.answer: The overall vacancy share includes all vacant housing units. For a rental market measure, use a definition that isolates units offered for rent and the corresponding rental inventory. Table B25004 breaks vacancies down by status.

title: Texas Data Center Tax Incentives and Property Tax Abatements
description: Compare Texas data center sales tax exemptions with a signed Fort Worth property tax abatement. Verify tax bases, eligibility, deadlines, and actual credits.
coverAlt: Three separate evidence records for a data center tax review. Fort Worth’s signed agreement sets the local city rate, Tarrant County groups several tax accounts, and the Texas Comptroller certifies qualifying purchases.
coverCaption: A property tax agreement, an appraisal district or county tax record, and a purchase exemption answer different questions about a project’s costs.
intro: Texas data center incentives can affect the annual property tax bill and the sales tax charged on eligible purchases. Start with the signed agreement for the affected taxing unit and the Comptroller’s certification for the facility and purchaser. Fort Worth’s signed 2019 Winner LLC expansion agreement set a 20% city abatement for tax year 2022 on specified taxes, subject to investment and completion evidence. That city agreement and the state sales tax program have separate requirements.
takeaways: For a local abatement, record the taxing unit, affected property, base year, covered tax years, conditions, and any remedy for missed commitments.
For a Texas sales tax exemption, identify the statutory section, facility certification, purchaser registration, and eligible cost items.
For underwriting, separate the signed rate and the county’s reported actuals. Tarrant County reports Winner LLC’s combined amounts without assigning the actual credit to the 2019 expansion.

sections.heading: Which records prove a data center tax incentive?

rows: Chapter 312 property tax abatement
The property and tax years a city or county agreed to abate, with performance conditions.
Signed agreement and amendments, legal description or account IDs, applicable taxing unit and tax year, appraisal and tax bill.
Chapter 380 or 381 economic development agreement
Any separately negotiated grant or rebate and the documented basis for payment.
Executed agreement, payment formula, compliance reports, term, and actual disbursements.
Texas data center sales tax exemption
A qualifying facility and registered party can claim exemption on eligible purchases under the applicable section.
Comptroller certification date, facility and purchaser registration numbers, Form 01-929, and invoices that identify the qualified costs.

blocks.text: Search the Comptroller’s local agreement database by jurisdiction and legal entity, then pull the controlling agreement and any amendments from the municipality or county. Search the appraisal district and collector records for the property tax account. Keep a credit against assessed property and a separate economic development payment in separate lines of the pro forma.

sections.heading: What did the signed Fort Worth expansion agreement cover?

blocks.text: Fort Worth City Secretary Contract 52160 was signed by Winner LLC on April 8, 2019, and by the city on April 10, 2019. For 2022 it set a 20% abatement on city real property taxes attributable to the increase over 2019 values and on city taxes on qualifying new tangible personal property. The contract cites the separate city economic development agreement, Contract 46728 as amended. Read each agreement against the land and work it covers.

The city required a Certificate of Completion for the real and personal property commitments. The signed agreement set baseline thresholds of $50 million of construction cost and $100 million of qualifying new tangible personal property cost, with defined adjustments requiring written approval. It reduced the rate to 10% when the company missed the commitment to spend 15% of construction costs with certified minority- or woman-owned businesses. Section 7.11 describes recovery of city taxes in the event of termination for failure to obtain the completion certificate.

Tarrant County’s separate report lists order 130032 with maximum rates of 60% for the county and 40% for the hospital district, a ten-year term, and a planned 2022 start. Its February 12, 2026 table reports $16,431,992.54 in county abatements and $10,708,657.83 in hospital district abatements on the combined Winner accounts, excluding tax year 2025. Those amounts sit on the original agreement row, with later rows marked as combined. The report does not isolate an actual credit for order 130032.

blocks.label: Download the agreement terms, county reporting scope, and Texas eligibility rules

sections.heading: What are the Texas data center sales tax exemption requirements?

rows: §151.359 · Qualifying data center
At least 100,000 sq ft in a single building or portion, 20 qualifying jobs, and at least $200 million of eligible investment over five years from certification.
Eligible purchases are exempt from state sales and use tax. Applicable local sales and use tax still applies.
§151.3595 · Qualifying large data center project

At least 250,000 sq ft on a single or eligible contiguous parcel group, 40 qualifying jobs, and at least $500 million of eligible investment over five years. The applicant must agree to contract for at least 20 MW of transmission capacity.
Form 01-929 specifies state and local tax exemption for this section. The statute starts the investment period at the earlier of application or certification.

blocks.text: Both pathways require a qualifying single occupant and facility and purchaser registrations. Eligible costs can include servers, electrical and cooling systems, and qualifying electricity. Review the statutory exclusions for general office or maintenance supplies, certain property incorporated into real estate, and short-term rentals. Source each invoice and determine who claims it.

Check the section on the certificate when reconciling the state guidance. The Comptroller’s web overview repeats state-only wording under the large-project heading and describes the investment period from certification. Form 01-929 distinguishes the two sections’ tax scope, and §151.3595(d)(2)(B) sets the earlier-of clock for large projects. Get the applicable treatment confirmed for the project before including the exemption in a budget.

sections.heading: How do I model the incentive for a site or loan?

blocks.text: Set up annual property tax lines by taxing unit and asset class. Start with the applicable taxable base, then apply the verified contract terms for each tax year. Use the assessor or collector record to corroborate any realized benefit. Put purchases and utility charges on a separate schedule and link each exemption to its certification and invoices.

Use Invariant Earth’s parcel identifier, boundary, and source fields to check which tract you are reviewing. Join the agreement’s legal description and tax accounts against the appraisal district records before applying the terms to the parcel or facility. Examine extensions, remedies and assignment language with the documents for the current transaction.

faqs.question: How do I find a Texas data center property tax abatement agreement?
faqs.answer: Start with the Comptroller’s local development agreement search and the city or county contract archive. Obtain the signed agreement, all amendments, the legal description, and the relevant tax accounts before estimating the benefit.

faqs.question: Does a city property tax abatement make equipment purchases exempt from Texas sales tax?
faqs.answer: Texas sales tax treatment requires the applicable Comptroller facility and purchaser registrations and Form 01-929. Verify the eligible property and statutory section for the purchase separately from the city’s agreement.

faqs.question: How do I verify whether an abatement was actually received?
faqs.answer: Get appraisal or collector records for the relevant account and tax year, and compare them with compliance records or reported amounts. A combined disclosure such as Tarrant County’s Winner LLC row cannot give an actual amount for one expansion by itself.

title: How to Track Proposed Data Center Projects Before Construction
description: Find early project leads in public agendas, approvals and permits. Compare four Loudoun developments and download eight verified application milestones.
coverAlt: Four Loudoun developments with different application outcomes. Golden Substation was approved with conditions, Quantum Park’s amendment was denied, Dulles North had two separate outcomes, and Dulles Technology Park was forwarded for later action.
coverCaption: Selected Loudoun County Board actions from October 20 through November 12, 2026. Each outcome applies to the specific application in the record.
intro: To find proposed data center or industrial projects before construction, start with local planning applications, hearing agendas, and staff reports. Then use the action report, recorded vote, or issued permit to confirm what moved forward. In Loudoun County, Golden Substation went from a scheduling motion in October to approval with conditions in November. At Dulles North Technology Park, the Board upheld a substation permit denial while moving the campus rezoning and two special exceptions to a later meeting.
takeaways: Save the jurisdiction, parent case ID and specific application ID. A campus may have separate dockets for the planned use, substation, access or utilities.
Record a scheduled hearing, approval, issued permit, contract award and construction start as distinct events. Attach the source and date to each one.
For contractor or equipment leads, look for a current scope and the evidence that somebody can buy it, such as a solicitation, award, permit or direct confirmation from the owner.

sections.heading: Where can I find early construction project leads?

rows: What is being proposed?
Planning application portal, public notices, hearing agenda and staff packet.
The proposed use, parent case, location, scope and review schedule where published.
What moved forward?
Meeting action report or approved minutes, recorded vote and decision attachment.
The action taken, the specific application it covers, any conditions and the announced next milestone.
Can the work proceed or go to bid?
Site plan or building permit system, procurement notice, bid tabulation or award for the relevant scope.
Whether an authority issued the specific permit or an owner solicited or awarded a defined package. Check each record’s scope and date.
How large is spending in this market?
Census construction spending estimates, alongside individual project or award records.
How much construction work was put in place in the reporting period. Use the project records to identify the work and counterparties.

blocks.text: Loudoun posts legislative land-use materials in its meetings archive and tracks permits and land development applications in LandMARC. Start with the exact case number. Read the final motion or case disposition once it is available, then open the conditions and later permits tied to that site and scope.

sections.heading: Four projects show why a headline status can mislead

blocks.text: We reviewed two county action reports and the November 12 hearing agenda and recording. The sample covers four named developments and eight records. It follows the dockets within those records, including separate decisions on the same site.

rows: Golden Substation · LEGI-2025-0012
The Board moved consideration from December 1 to November 5, then approved the three special exceptions 6–3 on November 5, subject to conditions dated July 10, 2026.
Read the conditions and follow the site plan and permit records for the proposed work.
Quantum Park · ZCPA-2023-0008
On October 20, the Board denied the requested concept plan amendment 7–2. Its findings addressed the proposed substation, campus compatibility, and off-site electrical impacts.
Keep the denial on that amendment. Check for a revised filing or record covering a different scope.
Dulles North Technology Park · CMPT-2025-0009
The Board affirmed the Planning Commission’s denial of the substation commission permit on November 12.
Track the specific substation docket and look for a later application or revised utility plan.
Dulles North Technology Park · ZMAP-2024-0017 and two special exceptions
The Board separately sent the rezoning and two special exceptions to its second March 2027 business meeting for action.
Monitor the March agenda and the later Board disposition. Keep the campus docket separate from the substation appeal.
Dulles Technology Park · ZMAP-2024-0018
The November 12 agenda listed this separate zoning conversion. The Board sent it to its second March 2027 business meeting for action.
Keep the applicant and case ID distinct from Dulles North and check the published agenda for the decision date.

blocks.label: Download eight dated project events, application IDs, and source references

sections.heading: How do I turn these records into a project watchlist?

blocks.text: Create one project key per jurisdiction and parent application. Keep the affected child application IDs on each event. Store the meeting or record date, the exact motion or disposition, who published it, and the next milestone where stated. Keep a page number for a PDF or a timestamp for a recording. Append new evidence when the project changes so you can see which scope cleared review and when.

For weekly construction prospecting, use new filings to spot work early. Recheck the action report before you count an approval, then look for bid dates, permit records, or owner confirmation before investing in a proposal. A site selector can use the same record to check the entitlement path, and an investor can tie each commitment to the application or agreement it depends on.

Use Invariant Earth to look up the mapped parcel, published zoning code, and nearby grid infrastructure once you have the site location. Keep the official decision with the case it describes. When a campus spans multiple tracts, use the filed maps and parcel identifiers to confirm which land the decision covers.

faqs.question: Where can I find proposed data center projects before construction?
faqs.answer: Search the local planning application portal and Board or Planning Commission packets. Start with the listed project and case number. Follow the decision report, site plan and permit records for the relevant scope.

faqs.question: Does a planning commission recommendation approve a project?
faqs.answer: Check which body has authority over the application. A recommendation goes to the decision maker. Read the later disposition for the same docket, including any conditions.

faqs.question: Can a data center and its substation have different approval statuses?
faqs.answer: Yes. The November 12, 2026 Dulles North hearing illustrates how separate applications can diverge. The Loudoun Board upheld the substation commission permit denial and sent the rezoning and two special exceptions to a later meeting.

title: ERCOT Day-Ahead and Real-Time Price Data
description: Download ERCOT historical hub prices and compare day-ahead and real-time settlement intervals. Reproduce the 25-hour Houston and West hub example.
coverAlt: Day-ahead and real-time electricity price lines for the Houston and West trading hubs on November 2, 2025. The two 02:00 intervals appear side by side in a shaded band.
coverCaption: ERCOT’s Houston and West hub settlement prices across the November 2, 2025 operating day. Real-time points are hourly means of four 15-minute prices.
intro: Download the Electric Reliability Council of Texas’s historical hub and load zone workbooks to compare day-ahead and real-time settlement prices. Keep the repeated-hour flag in your join. On November 2, 2025, the Houston hub had two periods labeled 02:00. Their day-ahead prices were $45.35 and $46.86 per MWh, and their real-time hourly means were $42.62 and $30.07. Dropping the second period understates the real-time wholesale energy value for a flat 1 MW load by $30.07 that day.
takeaways: Match on operating date, settlement point, hour ending, and repeated-hour flag. Retain the interval number for 15-minute real-time prices.
Weight real-time prices by energy used in each interval when modeling a changing load. A simple hourly average is appropriate for a load that stays constant within that hour.
Use ERCOT price and load archives for market analysis. Invariant Earth can identify the mapped utility territory and report the state’s average industrial retail price for context.

sections.heading: Where can I download ERCOT wholesale power market data?

rows: Historical hub or load zone prices
Download report 13060 for day-ahead and 13061 for real-time by calendar year.
Operating date, settlement point, market, hour ending, repeated-hour flag, interval, and archive vintage.
Resource-node or recent prices
Use the public day-ahead settlement price report and the 15-minute real-time report for resource nodes, hubs, and load zones. ERCOT’s Data Access Portal also provides access to covered reports.
Exact settlement point and product. A five-minute dispatch price and a 15-minute settlement price represent different records.
Actual system demand and forecasts
Use ERCOT’s Hourly Load Data Archives for actual weather-zone and system demand. The load page lists forecast-zone and weather-zone products.
Zone definition, actual or forecast status, interval, and forecast issue time where available.

blocks.text: An ERCOT trading hub price can support a wholesale comparison or a hedge benchmark. Use the settlement point named in the contract or settlement records when evaluating a specific exposure. Match geographic definitions before combining price, system demand, weather zones, or site-level meter data.

sections.heading: How do I handle the ERCOT repeated hour?

blocks.text: ERCOT published 25 hourly day-ahead prices and 100 quarter-hour real-time observations per hub on November 2, 2025. The 02:00 label appears twice, first with Repeated Hour Flag N and then with Y. In UTC, the normal occurrence ran from 06:00 to 07:00 and the repeated occurrence from 07:00 to 08:00. Preserve the original operating date and market label alongside the UTC boundaries.

blocks.text: To reproduce the comparison, select the Nov tab in each workbook. Filter to HB_HOUSTON and HB_WEST on November 2. Keep all four real-time intervals for every hour and flag. The repeated Houston hour’s prices were $29.21, $29.34, $30.35, and $31.37 per MWh. Their mean is $30.0675 per MWh. On an operating day with a clock change, compare the count with the actual market-day duration before filling or dropping any row.

blocks.label: Download 50 aligned hourly records, 200 interval prices, and workbook fingerprints

sections.heading: What does the market comparison tell a buyer?

blocks.text: For a flat 1 MW over the 25-hour operating day, compare what the same 25 MWh would be worth under the two price series. At Houston, the day-ahead series gives $808.25 and the real-time series gives $572.44. At West, the values are $853.03 and $510.04. A real settlement depends on scheduled and metered volumes, contract terms, and the applicable settlement point. The example isolates the two price series from those other variables.

For an industrial site shortlist, use Invariant Earth to get mapped utility territory and the published statewide industrial retail average. The state average and hub series serve different purposes. To budget a particular site, get the applicable tariff and supplier terms, then model demand charges, delivery costs, and any price index against the expected load shape and service dates.
Record the market design vintage before comparing prices across years. This example predates ERCOT’s December 5, 2025 launch of Real-Time Co-optimization Plus Batteries.

faqs.question: Where can I download ERCOT historical day-ahead and real-time prices?
faqs.answer: Use report 13060 for day-ahead hub and load zone prices and report 13061 for real-time. ERCOT publishes both as calendar-year workbooks. Use the separate settlement price reports for resource-node detail.

faqs.question: Why does ERCOT have two 02:00 prices on November 2, 2025?
faqs.answer: Texas clocks returned to standard time, giving ERCOT a 25-hour operating day. ERCOT’s price workbooks flag the second period labeled 02:00 with Y. Keep that flag in the key or convert each interval to unambiguous UTC boundaries.

faqs.question: How do I compare hourly day-ahead prices with 15-minute real-time prices?
faqs.answer: Match the same point and market hour first. Average four equal real-time intervals for a flat within-hour load. For varying load, calculate a price times MWh for every real-time interval and sum those values.

title: County Manufacturing Employment Data from BLS QCEW
description: Download county manufacturing jobs and establishment counts. Compare three Detroit-area counties, reproduce their location quotients and handle suppressed values.
coverAlt: Historic aerial photograph of Ford’s River Rouge industrial complex, the Rouge River and surrounding rail yards.
coverCaption: Ford’s River Rouge complex, circa 1927. Detroit Publishing Company collection, Library of Congress.
intro: For county manufacturing employment, start with the Bureau of Labor Statistics’ Quarterly Census of Employment and Wages. It gives you worksite jobs, establishment counts and industry concentration. In March 2026, Wayne County, Michigan, had 45,124 private transportation equipment manufacturing jobs, the most among the three counties we checked. Macomb County had fewer jobs at 31,414 and the strongest concentration at 8.52 times the national share. Use Invariant Earth to bring broader county employment and physical site evidence into the same shortlist.
takeaways: Compare employment, establishment counts and industry concentration together. They tell you how large the cluster is, how many operating locations it contains and how specialized the local economy is.
Use the same industry code, ownership class and reference month across counties and years. Check the code definition when crossing a classification change.
Preserve suppressed employment values as missing. In early 2026, Macomb County had five published motor vehicle manufacturing establishments and a suppressed job count.

sections.heading: Where can I download manufacturing jobs by county?

blocks.text: Download a county-area CSV from BLS Open Data Access and use the area code, quarter and industry code as part of the record key. For the figures below, we took quarter one of 2024, 2025 and 2026 and used the third month’s employment, the quarter’s establishment count and the third month’s employment location quotient. Select NAICS 31–33 for manufacturing, 336 for transportation equipment manufacturing or 3361 for motor vehicle manufacturing. Our industry rows use private ownership and all establishment sizes.

QCEW employment counts covered jobs at the workplace in the pay period that includes the 12th of the month. Establishments generally correspond to operating locations, and one firm can have several. For a hiring plan, add occupation data, wages and the drive-time labor shed around the candidate site.

sections.heading: Which Detroit-area county has the strongest manufacturing cluster?

blocks.text: We compared Macomb, Oakland and Wayne on the same NAICS 336 definition. Wayne led in total jobs in March 2026. Macomb had the highest location quotient. Oakland’s establishment count rose from 218 to 241 between the first quarters of 2024 and 2026 while March jobs fell from 22,514 to 20,729. Track both measures when deciding whether to investigate plant expansions, hiring or the depth of the local supplier base.

rows: Macomb
Oakland
Wayne

blocks.text: A location quotient divides the industry’s share of all county jobs by its share of all U.S. jobs. BLS uses all industries and ownership classes for both totals. The March 2026 U.S. share for private transportation equipment manufacturing was about 1.12%, based on 1,736,688 industry jobs and 154,771,941 total jobs. A quotient of 8.52 means the industry represented 8.52 times the national share in Macomb.

sections.heading: How should I handle suppressed manufacturing employment?

blocks.text: The narrower motor vehicle manufacturing code changes the picture. Wayne had 29 establishments and 24,244 jobs under NAICS 3361 in the first quarter of 2026. Oakland had 17 establishments and 853 jobs. Macomb published five establishments and withheld employment. We kept the latter value as null. Check both employment and location quotient disclosure fields before reading numeric placeholders, and remember that the broader NAICS 336 total already includes 3361.

When you need a continuous series, look for a broader industry or geography that BLS discloses across the full comparison period. Make that scope visible in the results. For a multi-year comparison, also confirm the industry definition and source vintage. BLS revises its quarterly releases, and changes in reporting geography or industry can move employment between categories.

blocks.label: Download the 12 BLS county and U.S. extracts with source links and disclosure flags

sections.heading: How do I turn these counts into a manufacturing shortlist?

blocks.text: Use job counts to size the existing cluster and location quotients to find specializations you might miss by sorting on job volume. Economic developers can compare the profiles with peer markets. Manufacturers can use them to pick areas for labor, supplier and freight diligence. Industrial investors can pair multi-year employment and establishment trends with project announcements, lease evidence and proposed construction before underwriting demand.

Invariant Earth’s public field catalog includes countywide annual employment and year-over-year change, parcel IDs and distance to a mapped mainline rail corridor. Pair those fields with the detailed BLS extracts when moving from a county screen to named tracts. For each finalist, verify the usable land, serving railroad and utility commitments against what the facility needs and when it needs it.

faqs.question: What is the best public source for manufacturing employment by U.S. county?
faqs.answer: BLS QCEW provides monthly employment and quarterly establishment counts by county and industry. Download a county-area CSV and filter to the NAICS detail and ownership class you need.

faqs.question: What does a manufacturing location quotient above 1 mean?
faqs.answer: The industry makes up a larger share of the county’s jobs than it does nationally. Use the employment count alongside the quotient to compare cluster size.

faqs.question: What does an N in QCEW disclosure code mean?
faqs.answer: BLS withheld that measure. Preserve the disclosure flag and store employment as missing when the flag applies, even when the CSV contains a zero placeholder. Keep any separately published establishment count.
