title: Historical Hourly Weather Data for Data Center Cooling
description: Compare NOAA hourly temperature and dew point before modeling data center cooling. Reproduce the Phoenix and Dulles results for 2023 to 2025.
coverAlt: A Landsat mosaic of the Phoenix metropolitan area showing its street grid, irrigated green fields and surrounding desert.
coverCaption: Phoenix metropolitan area from Landsat 9 imagery acquired July 3 and July 10, 2024. U.S. Geological Survey.
intro: Use Invariant Earth to compare the climate fields on a site shortlist. Use NOAA’s historical hourly station observations to see how heat and humidity varied before modeling a cooling system. In 2024, Phoenix Sky Harbor recorded 2,149 sampled hours at or above 95°F, compared with 86 at Washington Dulles. Dulles had 981 sampled hours with a dew point at or above 68°F, compared with 67 at Phoenix. The comparison uses outdoor weather at two airports and keeps missing hours visible.
takeaways: Measure dry-bulb temperature and dew point together. Dry-bulb temperature describes the air temperature. Dew point describes its moisture content.
Keep time zone, station ID, report type, quality flags and the number of paired hours. A tally of reports can count the same hour more than once.
Use site-specific design weather, equipment performance and water constraints to evaluate cooling options. The example thresholds here are for comparison.

sections.heading: Where can I download historical hourly temperature and humidity?

blocks.text: Use NOAA NCEI’s GHCNh station files for observed temperature and dew point. NCEI publishes station-year pipe-delimited files and lists Parquet downloads. GHCNh replaces the older Integrated Surface Dataset. Use NOAA’s U.S. Climate Normals when you need a long-term reference instead of observations from particular hours.

Choose a station that represents the site’s elevation and exposure. Keep the observation time in UTC until you intentionally convert to local time. This comparison counts each UTC calendar year and uses airport observations as regional screening examples.

sections.heading: What did the two stations record from 2023 to 2025?

blocks.text: We kept the last eligible routine aviation report in each UTC hour, requiring both dry-bulb temperature and dew point in the same record. We used NOAA’s documented passing quality codes and left unpaired hours missing. We counted 95°F air temperature and 68°F dew point separately and together. These round numbers make the two sites easy to compare.

rows: Phoenix Sky Harbor · 2023
Phoenix Sky Harbor · 2024
Phoenix Sky Harbor · 2025
Washington Dulles · 2023
Washington Dulles · 2024
Washington Dulles · 2025

blocks.text: Phoenix had 145 UTC hours without an eligible pair in 2025, and Dulles had 153. The separate heat and moisture comparisons that year hold even if every missing hour at the station with the lower count reached the corresponding threshold. The small counts for both conditions are more sensitive to missing observations.

blocks.label: Download the six station-year results, NOAA file links and quality rules

sections.heading: How do climate normals and outdoor observations fit into cooling design?

blocks.text: The 1991–2020 normal for the average July daily high is 106.5°F at Phoenix Sky Harbor and 87.6°F at Dulles. Use those values for a long-term baseline. An hourly series answers how often operating conditions co-occur, and the equipment model estimates what the plant consumes at those conditions.

For a design comparison, evaluate coincident dry-bulb and wet-bulb conditions, peak design weather, cooling equipment limits, and the expected IT load. Test water availability, backup operating modes and each design’s part-load behavior. Use outdoor station observations as weather inputs and apply the equipment’s own air and fluid requirements at the relevant operating points.

For an Invariant Earth screening workflow, start with the annual dry-bulb normal, the catalog’s wet-bulb design proxy and the count of hours at or below 15°C in a typical meteorological year. Use the last two as screening inputs with their source and method. Apply coincident hourly conditions and the project team’s design criteria before selecting equipment.

faqs.question: What hourly weather fields matter for a cooling study?
faqs.answer: Start with timestamped outdoor dry-bulb temperature, dew point and wet-bulb conditions, with station coverage and quality flags. Add the weather variables required by the equipment and operating mode being modeled.

faqs.question: Can I use NOAA’s monthly normals to estimate economizer hours?
faqs.answer: Monthly normals summarize typical conditions over a reference period. Estimate operating hours from coincident hourly weather and the controls and equipment limits of the proposed system.

faqs.question: How should I handle multiple airport reports in the same hour?
faqs.answer: Choose a consistent routine report and timing rule. For this comparison we require both temperatures in the same eligible report and take the last such report per UTC hour.

title: Freight Analysis Framework Data: FAF6 Downloads and Trade Flows
description: Download FAF6 freight data by state or metro area. Reproduce 2022 vehicle freight estimates for six Ohio destinations and compare them with border crossing counts.
coverAlt: Freight trucks crossing the Ambassador Bridge with the Detroit skyline behind them.
coverCaption: Ambassador Bridge, August 26, 2022. U.S. Customs and Border Protection photo by Charles Csavossy.
intro: Use the Freight Analysis Framework to compare estimated U.S. freight tonnage and value by origin, destination, mode and commodity. We used FAF6.0 to trace Canadian motorized vehicles and parts in 2022. An estimated 6.06 million tons entered the U.S. through Michigan. Of the roughly 419,265 tons that continued to Ohio, 52.4% went to two FAF regions around Cleveland and Columbus.
takeaways: For imports, the domestic origin field means where the cargo enters the U.S. The domestic destination is where that U.S. movement ends.
Use the BTS download or the tabulation tool for FAF estimates. Use the separate BTS Border Crossing Entry Data API if you need truck counts at a port.
Keep state remainder rows in the denominator when comparing how freight is distributed among metro areas.
Record the FAF version, estimate year, trade type, mode and units. FAF6.0 covers the 2022 benchmark. The earlier FAF5 release contains its own annual estimates and forecasts.

sections.heading: Where do I download U.S. freight flows?

blocks.text: Download the FAF6.0 state or regional CSV archive from the Bureau of Transportation Statistics, or use its Data Tabulation Tool to export filtered tables. Start with the state data for a statewide corridor comparison. Use FAF regions when a metro-area estimate matters. The 2022 state file reports thousands of tons and millions of 2022 dollars.

Keep the foreign mode and the domestic mode as separate columns. Imported freight can cross into the U.S. on one mode and continue on another. Treat rows in the Multiple Modes and Mail category as their own group. The category can include several kinds of transfers, so use a separate source to estimate the share using a specific terminal.

sections.heading: How much Canadian vehicle freight entered Michigan in 2022?

blocks.text: We filtered the FAF6.0 state CSV to imports, foreign origin Canada and SCTG code 36 for motorized and other vehicles, including parts. We then summed weight for four groups using the U.S. entry and destination fields. Each figure is a model estimate for 2022.

blocks.text: About 2.64 million tons entered through Michigan and went to other states. The 3.43 million tons that entered and ended in Michigan belong to both of the first two groups. Preserve the intersection when combining them. For site selection, compare the flows relevant to your proposed catchment and check the actual truck route or rail connection separately.

sections.heading: Which Ohio markets received the most vehicle freight?

blocks.text: The Cleveland–Akron–Canton freight region received an estimated 128,312 tons of Canadian vehicles and parts that entered through Michigan in 2022. The Columbus–Marion–Zanesville region followed at 91,465 tons. The rest-of-Ohio category also exceeded the Ohio portion of the Cincinnati region, so dropping the state remainder would hide a meaningful share of the flow.

blocks.text: In the FAF6 Data Tabulation Tool, select 2022 imports, Canada as the foreign origin, and commodity 36 for motorized and other vehicles including parts. Use regions as the level of geography. Select Michigan’s three U.S. entry regions and Ohio’s six domestic destination regions, including both state remainders. Keep all modes and report the weight by destination. The download includes the region codes, 30 matching regional rows and four matching state rows. The two files agree exactly before rounding, at about 419,265 tons and $1.532 billion in constant 2022 dollars.

Use the regional totals to decide which markets to investigate first. For a warehouse shortlist, verify routes to candidate gates, truck restrictions, rail service and customer locations separately. FAF estimates describe movement between regions and leave the exact crossing, route and facility unspecified.

sections.heading: How many trucks crossed at Detroit and Port Huron?

blocks.text: In the BTS Border Crossing Entry Data, 12 months of 2022 records add up to 1,414,853 inbound truck crossings at Detroit and 873,605 at Port Huron. These are counts at ports of entry across all cargoes. The FAF numbers above are weights for one commodity group across a state, including every mode represented in the state rows. Choose the measure that matches your question.

faqs.question: Is there a Freight Analysis Framework API?
faqs.answer: BTS publishes FAF6 through downloadable state and regional files and the online Data Tabulation Tool. The separate BTS Border Crossing Entry Data has a public API for port-level crossing counts.

faqs.question: What is the difference between a port of entry and the U.S. destination in FAF?
faqs.answer: The entry field records where imported goods enter the U.S. shipment segment. The U.S. destination records where that segment ends. The two can be in different states, as the Canada-to-Ohio flows through Michigan illustrate.

faqs.question: Can I use FAF6.0 to track year-over-year freight growth?
faqs.answer: FAF6.0 is a 2022 benchmark. For trends, use compatible annual records and document the version, geography and dollar basis. FAF5 has annual estimates and forecasts with a different benchmark and a constant-dollar base of 2017.

title: TxDOT Bid Results and Highway Contract Awards by CSJ
description: Find TxDOT bid results by CSJ. Compare low bids, award and rejection decisions, contractor names and construction status in three real Texas highway records.
coverAlt: Illustration of a concrete highway bridge carrying traffic beside a new span under construction.
coverCaption: AI-generated illustration of highway construction. The contract comparisons below use public TxDOT records.
intro: To verify a Texas highway contract award, find the controlling CSJ in the Texas Transportation Commission’s minute order and read the decision column in Exhibit A. A September 2026 summary listed a $2,623,266.87 low bid for US 287 in Tarrant County. The detailed exhibit shows a named bidder and the same amount under “Contract Amount,” alongside a REJECT decision. Keep that bid in your history and leave the award amount blank for that letting.
takeaways: Search by controlling CSJ and letting sequence. A later letting can give the same project a different bid and decision.
Keep the estimate, apparent low bid, award amount and payments in separate fields.
Use the notice to proceed or a recorded work-start date when you need evidence that construction can begin or has begun.

sections.heading: Where do I find TxDOT bid results and award decisions?

blocks.text: TxDOT’s letting page lists bidding notices, addenda, award results and bid tabulations. Find the controlling CSJ, or control-section-job number, in the proposal. Then keep the letting date and sequence number alongside it. The commission’s award or rejection comes after the bids are opened and reviewed.

sections.heading: How to use the TxDOT Project Tracker API by CSJ

blocks.text: Query the public ArcGIS layer for CONTROL_SECT_JOB. Preserve the leading zero and use the nine-digit text key, such as 017209047 for 0172-09-047. The exact query in the download requests route, project limits, status, contractor, stage and dated construction fields. Save the raw attributes and retrieval time alongside the dated minute-order decision.

The US 80 tracker row describes the westbound main lanes at Buffalo Creek and carries October 29 in its actual-let field. The October minute order describes October 6 and 7 as the bid-opening dates for the letting batch and October 29 as the date the order passed. Keep the tracker value as reported and confirm the individual opening date in the bid tabulation before using it in a timeline.

Use the route limits or project footprint to plan where to look for subcontracting work, deliveries or nearby properties. For a parcel screen in Invariant Earth, use a polygon that covers the documented work area and verify the resulting parcels against the plans. Keep construction start and contract status tied to agency evidence.

title: Federal Contract Awards API: USAspending, SAM.gov, and Site Data
description: Trace a federal construction solicitation to the signed award and its funding history. Compare SAM.gov and USAspending using Lock 25 and the New Lock at the Soo.
coverAlt: Cranes at the New Lock at the Soo construction site in Sault Ste. Marie, Michigan, at sunrise.
coverCaption: New Lock at the Soo on August 6, 2026. U.S. Army Corps of Engineers photo by Kelsie Hall.
intro: Use SAM.gov to check whether a bid is still open and read the amendments that affect your offer. After award, use USAspending to trace changes in obligations. At Lock and Dam 25, Amendment 0005 moved the published bid deadline from November 16 to December 9, 2026. At the New Lock at the Soo, the award notice listed $1.872 billion including options, while the initial signed obligation was about $1.068 billion.
takeaways: Search by place of performance for work in a market. Search by recipient location to find vendors based there.
Use an independently sourced coordinate or project boundary for an asset-level search in Invariant Earth. Keep the award ID, the location source and the date of each site record.
Track the generated award ID and use the transaction ID for individual actions. Add negative obligations, and keep zero-dollar changes when monitoring scope and schedule.
Keep the program budget, contract ceiling, net obligations and outlays as separate figures. Each answers a different spending question.

sections.heading: Which federal contract API should I use?

rows: Search public awards and measure obligations
Use USAspending’s spending-by-award search and pull the transaction history for each award.
Find current solicitations and published award notices
Use the SAM.gov Opportunities API with a public API key and check the latest active version. For earlier versions, use SAM.gov Data Services or the notice history.
Look up public procurement award and modification records
Use the SAM.gov Contract Awards API with the award or referenced contract identifier and a public API key.
Connect a known project site to its physical surroundings
Use Invariant Earth to retrieve parcel matches, mapped road and rail context, and source and vintage metadata from one U.S. coordinate.
Add procurement intelligence to a capture workflow
HigherGov offers a contract API for subscribers and an award search with place-of-performance filters.

blocks.text: For a regional pipeline, define the work geography and agency first, then filter the award and industry or service codes. For trade opportunities and subcontracting, verify the prime contractor and follow its procurement channels. An award record identifies the prime awardee. Current bidding opportunities are separate notices.

sections.heading: How do you check a federal construction bid deadline?

blocks.text: Search SAM.gov by solicitation number, notice type, agency and place of performance. A presolicitation or sources-sought notice can help you plan. Use the solicitation and its amendments to find the current requirements and deadline for an offer. The public Opportunities API returns the latest active version. Use notice history or SAM.gov Data Services for older versions.

For Lock and Dam 25 in Winfield, Missouri, both versions use solicitation W912P926RA004. The earlier notice shows November 16 as the original deadline. Amendment 0005 extended it to December 9, 2026 at 10 a.m. Central Standard Time. In the November 20 notice version we reviewed, Amendment 0007 also updated instructions to offerors and wage determinations. Use the current notice and attachments when preparing a bid.

sections.heading: How did the Soo Lock contract’s obligations change?

blocks.text: The Army Corps awarded the lock chamber construction contract on July 1, 2022. We queried the award W911XK22C0006 by its generated USAspending ID, then retrieved all rows from the transactions endpoint. This is the Phase 3 prime contract. The Army Corps describes the wider New Lock at the Soo project as a $3.219 billion investment in its September 2026 update.

The award API returns W911XK21R0001 under latest_transaction_contract_data.solicitation_identifier. SAM.gov uses that number for the presolicitation and includes it in the July 1, 2022 award notice for contract W911XK22C0006. Save the solicitation number and the signed contract identifier separately. For an order issued under a parent contract, retain the referenced parent ID as well.

rows: The initial award for construction of the new lock.
A change order extended the delivery date after an option was exercised.
December 15, 2023 · P00007
The transaction exercises Option 1B under the original contract.
A scope change at the monolith joints reduced the obligation.

blocks.text: The 91 actions included 75 increases, six decreases and ten with a recorded zero. The decreases reduced obligations by $1,940,055 in total. Summing all signed amounts exactly reproduces the award’s reported $1,938,479,275. The separate base-and-all-options field shows the $1,938,699,214 ceiling. Use the appropriate outlay field for amounts paid and check its accounting coverage and reporting date.

The $1.872 billion figure in the July 2022 SAM.gov notice includes the base and all options at the time of award. The award response checked November 24, 2026 gives $1,938,699,214 for that field and $1,938,479,275 in net signed obligations. For Option 1B, the Corps announced $213.8 million on December 21, 2023. The December 15 action P00007 records $210,189,500 obligated. Keep those as separate observations. The records do not explain the difference.

sections.heading: How do I search by job location instead of vendor location?

blocks.text: The award lists Sault Ste. Marie, Michigan, as its primary place of performance and Westerville, Ohio, as its recipient location. We ran the same contract search three times. Michigan as place of performance returned the award. Ohio as place of performance returned zero matches. Ohio as recipient location returned the award. Keep the contract ID, location field, retrieval date and signed actions with each result so you can replay the search when a modification arrives. The Soo Locks award identifies Chippewa County, Michigan. To check the site itself, obtain a coordinate or footprint from a separate project document.

sections.heading: How do I connect an award to a project site in Invariant Earth?

blocks.text: Start with the project map or permit drawing. For the New Lock at the Soo, we compared a Coast Guard navigation reference for the lock complex with the map center of an Army Corps storm-sewer easement exhibit. We converted both published coordinates to decimal degrees and intersected them with the Census Bureau’s 2026 county layer. Both points matched Chippewa County, FIPS 26033, and the two points were 484 meters apart.

That is enough to place both references in the award’s county. For a contractor checking a truck entrance or an analyst screening the parcels touched by construction, use the actual entrance or work boundary from the project drawings. The Coast Guard point describes the lock complex, and the easement exhibit describes separate work.

The worksheet contains two request bodies for Invariant Earth’s fetch endpoint. Each requests the parcel ID, parcel match type, nearest major road and distance to mapped rail. Keep each field’s status, source and vintage with the result. Check the match type before linking a parcel to the award, and confirm truck access and usable rail service with project or operator records. We checked the field names against the public catalog. Running the requests requires an API key.

faqs.question: How do I find the original solicitation for a federal contract award?
faqs.answer: Find the solicitation identifier in the award record and search it in SAM.gov, including archived notices. The USAspending detail for W911XK22C0006 returns W911XK21R0001, the same number the July 2022 SAM.gov award notice references. Save both identifiers so later contract modifications stay attached to the signed award.

faqs.question: Is there a free API for federal contract awards?
faqs.answer: USAspending’s public API provides award details and transaction history. SAM.gov also offers public opportunities and contract award APIs that require an API key.

faqs.question: How do I calculate cumulative contract obligations?
faqs.answer: Fetch each transaction for the award and sum the signed federal action obligation values. Deobligations reduce the total. Retain the transaction ID and action date, and compare the full result to the award’s reported total obligation.

faqs.question: What is the difference between a contract ceiling and an obligation?
faqs.answer: The ceiling is the potential award value, including all options as reported. The obligation is the amount the government has legally committed. An outlay records payment.

faqs.question: How do I find federal infrastructure contract awards near me?
faqs.answer: In USAspending, apply a place-of-performance filter and narrow by award type, time period, agency or relevant industry codes. Confirm the work location in the award detail or project record.

faqs.question: Can Invariant Earth find the construction location from a federal contract number?
faqs.answer: Start with USAspending or SAM.gov for the contract and the reported place of performance. Confirm the specific site with an agency map, permit or drawing. Pass that verified coordinate to Invariant Earth for cited parcel and transportation data.

title: FEMA Flood Claims Data API: NFIP v3 and County-Level Losses
description: Use OpenFEMA’s current NFIP claims API. Compare Hurricane Ida records and net flood payments in two counties and download the reproducible totals.
coverAlt: Hurricane Ida’s clouds and eye seen from the International Space Station, with the station’s robotic arm in the foreground.
coverCaption: Hurricane Ida seen from the International Space Station. Photograph from NASA.
intro: Use Invariant Earth to check the FEMA flood map at a U.S. site, then use OpenFEMA’s NFIP Redacted Claims v3 to study payment history at county scale. In FEMA’s November 2026 extract, rows tagged to Hurricane Ida in the period we checked sum to about $290.6 million in net building payments in St. John the Baptist Parish, Louisiana, and $63.8 million in Bergen County, New Jersey. The totals describe payments in the federal insurance program and the same storm has a different event code in each state.
takeaways: Use the current endpoint, /api/open/v3/NfipClaims. We tested it on November 23, 2026 and received a valid response. The old FimaNfipClaims v2 endpoint returned 404.
For event analysis, use the loss date, reported county code and storm designation together. Keep rows with blank event tags in a separate count.
Keep building, contents and Increased Cost of Compliance payments in separate fields. Retain the data vintage and use the published county field for geography.

sections.heading: Where do I get FEMA flood insurance claims data?

blocks.text: The live endpoint is https://www.fema.gov/api/open/v3/NfipClaims. Start with countyCode, dateOfLoss, floodEvent, eventDesignationNumber and netBuildingPaymentAmount. Request asOfDate with the data. The OpenFEMA catalog reports the refresh date separately and describes a monthly publication with a lag behind the system of record.

For reproducible totals, filter by the Census county FIPS code and use an inclusive start and exclusive end date. Request a total count with $inlinecount, sort by id and fetch the remaining pages. Check for duplicate record IDs and confirm that the page counts match FEMA’s reported total in a consistent extract.

sections.heading: What did NFIP pay after Hurricane Ida in two counties?

blocks.text: The National Hurricane Center documents Ida’s Louisiana landfall and later flooding in New Jersey. We selected loss dates from August 28 through September 4, 2021, and counted rows tagged Hurricane Ida within that window. All matching rows in these samples show an asOfDate of November 16, 2026. Amounts in the table are net payments after recovery, rounded to the nearest thousand dollars.

rows: St. John the Baptist Parish, Louisiana
Bergen County, New Jersey

blocks.text: A date-only filter returned nine more rows in the Louisiana parish and twenty more in Bergen County. Those rows carried blank event labels in this extract. The benchmark preserves their contribution to the window total separately. There were 3,227 and 1,515 Ida-tagged rows with a positive net building payment, respectively. Use that count when your question is how many records show a positive building payment.

blocks.label: Download county totals, exact API queries and calculation notes

sections.heading: How should a risk team interpret those totals?

blocks.text: The NFIP series reflects losses reported to the federal program. The amount paid depends on the properties that were insured, claims made, and coverage and payment terms. A county payment total answers a different question from economic damage or the number of buildings that flooded. To compare areas across years, carry the reporting vintage, insurance participation and the geography along with the result.

For county reporting, use countyCode rather than assigning records geographically from rounded coordinates. FEMA intentionally reduces coordinate precision for privacy. Use the appropriate flood map edition or modeled hazard evidence to assess the footprint of a particular building. Invariant Earth publishes point-level FEMA fields with their source and vintage. The map and claims aggregate belong in separate measures.

faqs.question: What replaced the FEMA FimaNfipClaims v2 API?
faqs.answer: Use OpenFEMA’s v3 NfipClaims resource at https://www.fema.gov/api/open/v3/NfipClaims. The resource name changed as well as the version in the path.

faqs.question: Can I look up a building’s claim history by address in the public file?
faqs.answer: The public file is redacted. FEMA rounds latitude and longitude to one decimal place for privacy and recommends using its published county and state fields for aggregation.

faqs.question: What is the difference between gross and net building payment?
faqs.answer: OpenFEMA describes netBuildingPaymentAmount as amountPaidOnBuildingClaim less recoveries. Keep the field name with the total and distinguish it from payments for contents or Increased Cost of Compliance.

faqs.question: How do I count flood claims tied to the same hurricane in different states?
faqs.answer: Use the reported storm name and loss date window, then check the event designation in each state. In these Ida queries FEMA used LA0421 and NJ0421. Report rows with blank codes separately.

title: Building Footprint Data APIs and Open Datasets
description: Compare Invariant Earth, LightBox, Overture Maps and Microsoft. Test building footprints by address with a Brooklyn Navy Yard mismatch and three NYC polygons.
coverAlt: 2024 overhead photograph of industrial buildings along Flushing Avenue at the Brooklyn Navy Yard.
coverCaption: Brooklyn Navy Yard along Flushing Avenue. Aerial imagery from NYS ITS Geospatial Services, 2024.
intro: Use Invariant Earth when you need building footprint area in the same U.S. coordinate lookup as parcel boundaries, zoning and site hazards. For raw polygons, trial LightBox or download Overture Maps or Microsoft geometry. At Brooklyn Navy Yard, 63 Flushing Avenue is the operator’s address for Building 92. The city geocoder puts that address inside the polygon labeled 280. A lookup for the number 92 returns a different outline on the same tax lot.
takeaways: To get a footprint from an address, resolve the location, retrieve candidate polygons and confirm which structure the customer means. A campus street address can belong to several buildings.
Use a projected coordinate system to measure footprint area. Keep that area separate from gross floor area, insurable square footage and the measurements used for a replacement-cost estimate.
Run the same tests across the counties, building types and historical dates you actually need. Save the returned geometry, source and match decision so another person can reproduce it.

sections.heading: Which source should you start with?

blocks.text: Try primary_building_footprint_sqm and parcel_boundary_geojson together in Earth. The first measures the matched building outline and the second returns the land boundary. Request within_floodplain_polygon in the same lookup to see the FEMA result at the input coordinate. For a building-wide flood screen, intersect the verified building polygon with the flood layer.

Start with how your team will use the data. A live U.S. address workflow needs identifiers and a way to resolve ambiguous results. A regional GIS model needs bulk geometry, a dated release and clear reuse terms. This comparison uses public provider documentation. The Brooklyn test below uses city records independently.

rows: Invariant Earth
Combine Overture-derived footprint area and building characteristics with parcel geometry and other site fields. Each field includes its source.
Check the input coordinate and confirm the matched structure. The documented footprint-area field uses the containing building or the nearest one within 100 metres.
LightBox Structures API
U.S. building lookup by structure ID, parcel or geometry. Related addresses use linked LightBox identifiers.
Can you get all structures on a shared lot and identify which one matches the submission?
Overture Maps Buildings
Bulk GeoParquet for large areas. Parent buildings and building parts are published separately.
Can you track the same structure across releases and keep parts out of the building count? Check source attribution and ODbL terms.
Microsoft Global ML Building Footprints
Download imagery-derived outlines by region and grid tile when you can host and query the data yourself.
Review omissions, merged roofs and new development against imagery from a known date. Plan your own address and parcel join.
Local city or county GIS
Check government-issued identifiers, footprint attributes and linked local records where the authority publishes them.
Check the update date, placeholder geometries and how the source handles a building that spans multiple lots.

sections.heading: A street address can land inside the wrong footprint

blocks.text: We searched NYC GeoSearch for 141 and 63 Flushing Avenue in Brooklyn using the city’s Property Address Directory release 26c. We took each result with the requested house number, street and borough, then used its Building Identification Number (BIN) to query NYC Building Footprints. Both address points landed inside the footprint returned for their BIN. Both footprints carried the same base tax lot number, 3020230001.

rows: 141 Flushing Avenue, Building 77
BIN 3335143, city label 77
The operator’s building label and city result agree.
63 Flushing Avenue, Building 92
BIN 3335129, city label 280
The address point is inside this outline. The operator’s crosswalk lists former 280 as Building 140, a separate building from 92.
City lot and name lookup for 92
BIN 3335175, city label 92
Separate candidate polygon on the same lot. It does not contain the point returned for 63 Flushing Avenue.

blocks.text: The lot had 93 records coded as Building in the footprint layer on November 23, 2026. A parcel ID alone leaves many possible structures. For an insurance submission or appraisal at 63 Flushing Avenue, preserve both candidate IDs, compare the outlines with the operator map or a current plan and keep the match open until you can verify the intended building. The city describes its footprint name field as unmaintained, which makes the name match evidence to review.

blocks.label: Download the three footprints, two address points and source queries

sections.heading: How do you measure the area of a building footprint?

blocks.text: Measure the polygon in a local projected coordinate system with known units. We requested the NYC geometry in New York Long Island State Plane (EPSG:2263), then measured the enclosed area in square US survey feet. The outline for Building 77 measured about 61,676 square feet. NYC’s metadata advises against using the published Shape_Area value for this purpose.

A footprint measures horizontal extent. A multistory building can have much more floor area than its footprint, and a roof traced in an aerial image can overhang the walls. For lending, use the appraisal or building plan to check the area used for underwriting. For insurance, establish the insured building and get the construction details and dimensions that the replacement-cost method requires.

sections.heading: What should a provider prove in a trial?

blocks.text: Give every provider the same address list, parcels, building labels and known outcomes. Include a campus, a condo with a billing lot, a site with multiple sheds, and a property with a recorded demolition or addition. Ask for the original IDs, the polygons and the data vintage. Look at whether the system forwards uncertain matches for review and whether it can reproduce a result from the quote or credit date.

Score correct building matches, false matches and unresolved cases separately. Evaluate geometry only after verifying the structure. Compare candidate polygons against a trusted reference in the same projection. For a flood or zoning overlay, retain the exact footprint and map edition used so you can tell why the result changed after a new release.

faqs.question: Can I get a building footprint from a street address?
faqs.answer: Geocode the address, retrieve footprint candidates by building ID, parcel or location, and confirm which structure the address refers to. On a campus, add the building number or entrance and compare with the operator’s map or property plan.

faqs.question: Where can I download open building footprints in bulk?
faqs.answer: Overture Maps publishes Buildings in GeoParquet with a separate building parts layer. Microsoft publishes imagery-derived polygons in regional downloads. Check source attribution, licensing, the imagery or release date and local coverage before adopting either.

faqs.question: Is a footprint the same as a tax parcel?
faqs.answer: A footprint outlines a structure viewed from above. A tax parcel describes land for assessment and administration. Brooklyn Navy Yard’s lot 3020230001 had 93 records coded as Building in the NYC footprint layer for this check.

faqs.question: Can I use a building footprint for total square footage?
faqs.answer: Calculate the horizontal footprint area in a suitable projected coordinate system. Obtain gross floor area from building plans, an appraisal or an authoritative property record. A footprint leaves the number, size and use of floors open.

title: Building Permit Data APIs for Commercial Property
description: Compare Invariant Earth, Mireye, Shovels and other permit APIs. Test coverage by city, building matches, project counts and inspection dates.
coverAlt: Aerial photograph of the Brooklyn Army Terminal buildings, rooftop equipment and pier along the waterfront.
coverCaption: Brooklyn Army Terminal. Aerial imagery from NYS ITS Geospatial Services, 2024. The permit case uses NYC Department of Buildings records.
intro: Use Invariant Earth to connect permit research to a cited U.S. property record. One coordinate can return parcel identity and boundary, zoning, building characteristics and hazards. Join the original permit by building ID and verify its scope at the issuing agency. At Brooklyn Army Terminal, one fit-out appears as six permit rows, four work permits and three filings. Two other filings mention rooftop work and describe equipment replacement.
takeaways: Keep the building, parcel, job filing and work permit IDs. An address match alone can attach work to the wrong structure on a shared lot.
Record filing, issue, expiration and sign-off dates separately. A work description and a date only answer the question when they describe the right scope and milestone.
Test your provider on the authorities, years and property types in your portfolio before paying for a national feed.

sections.heading: Which building permit API fits the job?

blocks.text: Start in Invariant Earth with parcel_apn, parcel_match_type, parcel_zoning and primary_building_footprint_sqm. Use the parcel match to anchor your property file, then attach the original building, filing and permit IDs from the issuer. This lets you review work scope alongside the zoning and exposures at that location.

A portfolio monitoring team needs a way to search across markets and catch new records. A lender or underwriter reviewing one building needs the issuer’s record, the work scope and the status as of the credit or quote date. Use the table to choose what to trial. The comparisons use public provider documentation. The tests below query New York City and Seattle directly.

rows: Invariant Earth
Build a cited property record for permit diligence. Fetch the parcel, zoning, building features and hazards together by coordinate.
Check that the issuing agency’s building ID and work address refer to the structure you’re reviewing. Save the permit ID and the Earth field sources.
Mireye Permits
Search or count permits by area or parcel. Check office coverage and dates before querying.
Does the search cover the office, dates and work type you need? Can you retain both the source status and the normalized status?
Shovels
Search by geography and date range, with filters for work and property details.
Can you recover the original permit number and status for commercial work in each target jurisdiction?
West Kite
Request permits as part of a commercial property record or search for permits in an area.
Can you distinguish one building from another when both sit on the same tax lot?
ATTOM
Look up building permits within an existing ATTOM property integration.
Can you identify which event the effective date represents and recover separate dates needed for review?
PermitStack
Look up permit history by address or parcel. Inspect the individual permit rows behind the property’s derived signals.
For a roofing match, can you return the source permit and distinguish the issue date from the date inspections were completed?
Issuing agency
Look up the work permit, filing and applicable inspection or closeout record.
Which local systems and work types are covered, and what history does each system expose?

blocks.text: For procurement, give each provider the same sample buildings and compare its returned records with the issuer. Keep the provider’s documented coverage separate from the results you observe in the trial.

sections.heading: How do you check building permit API coverage by city?

blocks.text: Start with the issuing office, the milestone you care about and its date range. We checked Mireye’s public office summaries for New York City and Seattle on November 24, 2026. Then we counted permit numbers in each city’s own export for issue dates after the last date in the corresponding office summary, through November 23.

columns: Newer issue dates in the city export
rows: New York City
Partial. Latest date in the office summary was November 20.
777 rows and 665 distinct work permit numbers issued November 21 to 23.
Seattle
Partial. Latest date in the office summary was November 19.
9 rows and 9 distinct permit numbers issued November 20 to 23.

blocks.text: The date difference shows why a coverage check belongs in a trial. It compares the public office summaries with the cities’ exports. A licensed record-by-record search would establish which permits the vendor actually returns. For your own trial, use the same office, date field, work types and distinct permit ID on both sides. Save the retrieval date and track changes during the trial.

blocks.label: Download the New York and Seattle coverage check and exact source queries

sections.heading: One Brooklyn tenant fit-out, six rows and four work permits

blocks.text: We queried selected filings at 140 58th Street, the Brooklyn Army Terminal campus address. The selected rows share Building Identification Number 3414976 and tax lot 3057780001. The DOB NOW Approved Permits export returned six rows for the three filings below. The rows represent four distinct work permit numbers.

rows: General construction for an eighth-floor interior alteration, issued September 18, 2026.
1 row, 1 work permit
Plumbing and sprinkler changes for part of the eighth floor, issued October 15, 2026.
4 rows, 2 work permits
Mechanical systems work for the fit-out, issued September 18, 2026.
1 row, 1 work permit

blocks.text: The plumbing and sprinkler filing repeats each work permit number on two work type rows. Deduplicating by permit number gives four permits. Grouping by filing gives three filings. Keep the six source rows for scope analysis. Count one fit-out here because the related filings and their descriptions link the work. For a portfolio, spot-check the project grouping before you count projects from a shared filing prefix.

blocks.label: Download the Brooklyn permit and filing records

blocks.text: The download includes the exact NYC query URLs, selected source rows, retrieval timestamps and a hash of each returned response. It is a sample of known filing IDs and excludes other work at the Terminal. Repeating the queries later can return updated statuses.

sections.heading: A permit for rooftop equipment can look like a new roof

blocks.text: A keyword search for roof and replacement can pick up HVAC work. We joined two more DOB NOW job filings to their permit rows using the filing number. The city’s work type and the written scope provide more detail than the word roof alone.

columns: Dates and status in the exports
rows: Replacement of two rooftop HVAC units in their existing locations.
Permit issued December 6, 2022. The filing shows sign-off on December 27, 2022 and a Letter of Completion issued.
Replacement of rooftop chillers.
Permit issued October 24, 2022. The selected filing row has no sign-off date.

blocks.text: For a roof-age field, ask for the document that identifies the roof assembly or area replaced, plus evidence of completion. A sign-off on mechanical work closes out a different scope. When an export leaves a sign-off field blank, check the issuer’s full record before classifying the job as open.

sections.heading: Which Seattle roof permits show completed inspections?

blocks.text: Seattle defines its Completed Date as the date when all inspections for the permit were completed. We checked three nonresidential records on November 24, 2026. The permit category, work description and completion date each tell you something different.

rows: Alki Community Center, 6584417-CN
The Building category includes a 5,400-square-foot reroof and five anchors.
Issued March 23, 2017. Inspections completed March 20, 2018.
Meadowbrook Community Center, 7163023-RR
The Roof category describes a reroof.
Issued September 16, 2026. The export shows Issued and has no completion date.
Seattle University’s Lemieux Library, 6986192-CN
The Building category describes rooftop telecom and an equipment room.
Issued January 23, 2025. Inspections completed May 5, 2025 for that scope.

blocks.text: A Roof-only filter would miss Alki, and a rooftop keyword search would include the library’s telecom work. Carry Alki’s March 2018 date as permit inspection completion for the documented scope. To establish installation timing or remaining roof life, request the contractor’s completion documents and check which roof area they cover.

sections.heading: Which fields belong in a permit history?

rows: Issuing authority, source URL and retrieval timestamp
Use them to compare a later correction or export against the evidence available for an earlier decision.
Source address, matched building ID and parcel ID
Check which structure the permit applies to when one tax lot has multiple buildings or addresses.
Project reference, filing ID and work permit number
Count projects, submissions and permits at their own level. Keep scope lines attached to the permit.
Filed, approved, issued, expired, signed off and occupancy dates
Retain each milestone and the original status label. Keep the exact source date that supports each conclusion.
Work type, scope text and affected space
Separate a full roof replacement from an equipment swap and a building conversion from a single tenant alteration.

blocks.text: A current export can report an old issue date and a newer status in the same row. Store dated snapshots or issuer event records when your team needs to replay a decision. Label facts by when the agency says they took effect and when you retrieved them. For lender or insurer reviews, save the exact evidence used with the decision file.

items.label: Test permit alerts against dated San Francisco records

blocks.text: For historical New York City work, check both DOB NOW and the older Buildings Information System when the project calls for it. NYC’s main DOB NOW job filings dataset also omits certain work types that have separate feeds. A permit documents the construction scope. Where legal occupancy matters, check the applicable certificate and the spaces it covers.

sections.heading: Run a trial on buildings you already know

items: Start with the Brooklyn fit-out and the Seattle roof records above. Add a multi-building parcel and a job that predates the current local filing system in a market you cover.
Compare the building match, permit IDs and individual milestone dates. Ask how missing records and uncertain address matches are returned.
Reconcile one multi-trade job. Check whether the API returns rows, permits or projects when it reports a count.
Test the result you would actually use. For a roof field, ask for the replaced assembly and completion evidence. For legal use, request the occupancy document.
Confirm update lag, historical versions, bulk access and rights to retain the original evidence in your workflow.

faqs.question: How does Invariant Earth fit into building permit diligence?
faqs.answer: Use Invariant Earth to retrieve parcel identity, zoning, building characteristics and hazards together with sources. Link the issuer’s permit by its building and filing IDs to preserve the scope and dates of the work.

faqs.question: Which API should I use for building permits by address?
faqs.answer: Start with Invariant Earth for the cited parcel and building context. For permit records, compare Mireye and Shovels for area and date searches, West Kite for commercial property records, ATTOM within an ATTOM integration, and PermitStack for property permit history. Check the authority, dates, scope and coverage against the issuer.

faqs.question: Why does a building permit search return duplicate rows?
faqs.answer: An issuer can publish a row per work type or other part of the record. For the Brooklyn fit-out, six rows correspond to four distinct work permit numbers and three filings. Keep those counts separate.

faqs.question: Can I estimate roof replacement date from a permit?
faqs.answer: Match the permit to the correct building and check that its scope covers the roof assembly or area you are evaluating. Then look for a separate completion or inspection record. Rooftop equipment permits describe a different scope.

faqs.question: Does a building permit establish legal occupancy in NYC?
faqs.answer: Use the applicable Certificate of Occupancy or Temporary Certificate of Occupancy for legal use and occupancy coverage. Review which floors or spaces it applies to and any expiration or conditions.

title: Zoning data APIs for U.S. parcels and site selection
description: Compare zoning APIs and city GIS. Use NYC parcel tests to see how a lookup handles split zoning and a commercial overlay that covers part of a lot.
coverAlt: Aerial map of 2239 Forest Avenue in Staten Island. Five colored areas show the share of the tax lot in each base zoning district. The published point falls in C8-1.
coverCaption: 2239 Forest Avenue, Staten Island. The white line traces the MapPLUTO tax lot. Colors show the clipped NYC zoning polygons. Aerial imagery from USDA, USGS and The National Map.
intro: Use Invariant Earth to screen a U.S. location with a cited parcel ID, zoning code, parcel boundary and other site conditions in one lookup. Use city district geometry to measure zoning across a tract. For a U.S. parcel zoning lookup, compare Zoneomics for point and area queries, Gridics for development standards in supported jurisdictions, and Regrid for zoning fields attached to parcel records. Keep the local government’s map and ordinance as your reference. At one Staten Island address, a point lookup gives one district, the city’s tax lot record lists three, and a boundary overlay finds five.
takeaways: Decide whether you need zoning at a coordinate, a parcel summary, or each district intersecting the site.
Ask how the API handles small overlaps and where its source shows the adopted map and rule.
Verify the zoning lot, applicable rules and approvals with the local authority before committing to a use or floor area.

sections.heading: Which zoning API fits the work?

blocks.text: Give every provider the same parcel boundary and proposed use. The commercial comparison below uses published documentation. The five-district result comes from the city data queried for this article.

columns: What to check in a trial
rows: Zoneomics
Point and area lookups, with published options for use tables, controls and overlay data where available.
Submit the parcel polygon and ask for the geometry, source date and permitted-use reference for the affected portion.
Gridics
Parcel-level zoning, uses, setbacks and modeled development capacity.
Check jurisdiction coverage and ask which source rules and parcel assumptions drive a building envelope or floor-area result.
Regrid
Parcel IDs with local zoning codes, standardized categories on applicable plans and a matched zoning product.
Ask when you receive one parcel code, how the code is assigned and which product supplies more detail or a link to the city code.
Invariant Earth
A coordinate lookup returns parcel identity and a Regrid-sourced zoning code alongside other location fields.
Review the matched assessor parcel number. The published catalog allows a nearest-parcel fallback for parcel matching. Use the city district geometry to test the whole tract.
Municipal GIS and code
Local tax maps, district polygons, overlays and the adopted map and ordinance. Format and update process depend on the jurisdiction.
Confirm map and ordinance dates independently. Ask the authority which zoning lot and approvals apply to your plan.

sections.heading: One Staten Island parcel, three different lookup results

blocks.text: We used the MapPLUTO 26v2 boundary for 2239 Forest Avenue, Staten Island, borough-block-lot 5012500011. We also queried NYC Planning’s base zoning district polygons on November 23, 2026. The published parcel point falls in C8-1. MapPLUTO lists M1-1, C4-1 and C8-1 in that order and flags the parcel as split.

The polygon overlay finds five intersections. C4-1 and M1-1 each cover a little over 37% of the mapped tax lot. R3A and R3-2 together cover 7.17%. Both individual shares fall below the 10% minimum defined for MapPLUTO’s base district fields. The two largest districts switch order between the parcel fields and this overlay. The largest areas differ by only 0.35 percentage points in our calculation. Keep the original parcel fields and recomputed results with their own source dates.

rows: Largest overlap in the polygon calculation. MapPLUTO lists it second.
MapPLUTO lists it first.
Contains the published parcel point. MapPLUTO lists it third.
R3A
Appears in the geometry overlay.
Appears in the geometry overlay.

blocks.text: We projected the boundary and zoning polygons to New York State Plane Long Island in U.S. survey feet, intersected each district with the tax lot and divided by the mapped polygon area. The total is approximately 378,715 square feet. MapPLUTO’s separate LotArea field is 376,110 square feet. Use the polygon area as the denominator when reproducing these shares. Displayed percentages may differ from 100% because of rounding.

sections.heading: How do you check a commercial zoning overlay by address?

blocks.text: Match the address to its tax lot, then check the city’s commercial overlay layer for the site. In NYC, a C1 or C2 overlay can be mapped inside a residential district. The point tells you whether one location falls inside it. Intersect the overlay polygon with the lot to see how much of the site it covers, then compare the result with the space you plan to lease or build.

These three Union Street lots in Brooklyn share the R6A base district. We matched MapPLUTO 26v3 and the city’s Zoning Tax Lot Database by borough, block and lot, then measured the C1-4 overlap from the city’s GIS polygons on November 24, 2026.

blocks.text: At 682 Union Street, the point and tax lot record both return C1-4, but the mapped overlay stops partway through the lot. A retailer evaluating space toward the back needs to locate that space on a floor plan and verify the zoning lot, current use classification and any applicable limits or approvals. NYC’s retail and services provisions distinguish general allowances from uses that have size limits, other conditions or special permit requirements.

For a vendor trial, ask for the base district, overlay code and geometry as separate outputs. Invariant Earth’s parcel zoning field gives the sourced parcel code for the initial screen. Use the city geometries to test the overlay share and ask how the provider reports a confirmed absence or an unresolved lookup.

sections.heading: What should a zoning API return before you rely on it?

columns: What a usable result gives you
rows: Parcel identity
The exact boundary, assessor ID, match method and the coordinates used. A nearby match stays marked as nearby.
Districts and additional rules
Each base district and the geometry affecting the tract. Commercial overlays and special districts have their own records.
Which rules are in effect
The source map, ordinance section, effective date and any recent amendment. Keep a vendor’s refresh time in a separate field.
Proposed use
The local use classification and the approval process for the operation. A zoning district label alone leaves those questions open.
Site capacity
The zoning lot used in the calculation and any split-district rules, setbacks, height limits or approvals that change the result.

blocks.text: New York City defines a zoning lot separately from a tax lot. A zoning lot can include multiple lots of record under specified conditions. The city also has separate provisions when a zoning lot crosses district boundaries. Confirm the zoning lot and ask for a written determination when a lease, construction budget or loan depends on the result.

faqs.question: Can I get zoning by address from an API?
faqs.answer: Yes. Some APIs accept an address, then return the district at the matched point or a summary tied to the parcel. Ask which result you are getting and run a polygon check on split lots.

faqs.question: Why does one parcel have several zoning districts?
faqs.answer: A mapped district boundary can cross a tax lot. A polygon overlay returns the intersecting districts and their shares. A parcel summary may omit small intersections under its published reporting rules.

faqs.question: Can a property have a commercial overlay and a residential base district?
faqs.answer: Yes. NYC maps C1 and C2 overlays within residential districts. Check the official overlay polygon against the intended premises. At 682 Union Street, the published point is inside the C1-4 overlay and the polygon covers about 46.5% of the mapped tax lot.

faqs.question: Can I estimate buildable floor area from a zoning API?
faqs.answer: Use the API to screen a scenario. Verify the zoning lot, current rules, intended use and applicable approvals before applying a floor-area figure to a design or project budget.

title: EV charging station APIs for location and live availability
description: Compare AFDC, TomTom, HERE, Google Places and OCPI. Test EV charging APIs for correct port counts, live availability and shared charging power.
coverAlt: Aerial map of the I-70 and U.S. Route 42 interchange near London, Ohio, with Pilot 454 and TA London marked.
coverCaption: I-70 Exit 79 near London, Ohio. Pins use AFDC station coordinates. Aerial imagery from USGS, USDA and The National Map.
intro: Use Invariant Earth for site screening around a proposed charger location. One coordinate lookup can bring together parcel, road and utility context. Use charger feeds to plan trips and check connector availability. Use the U.S. Department of Energy’s AFDC API to locate charging stations and count installed ports. For a driver who needs a free connector now, use a timestamped availability feed from a mapping provider or charging network. The difference shows up at one Ohio interchange. The federal inventory lists 16 fast-charging ports across two stops. A routine sum of the equipment export returns 160 because it repeats the station total on each row.
takeaways: Count installed ports once per station ID. Preserve repeated equipment rows when the source supplies no equipment ID.
Keep connector compatibility, station access hours and live equipment status in separate fields.
Ask when the network observed the status. A station record can be updated today and still carry no occupancy data.

sections.heading: Which EV charging API should you use?

blocks.text: Start with the decision you need to support. A planner can use an inventory to find gaps in a corridor. A routing app needs to know whether a compatible charger is free and how recently that was observed. The commercial comparisons below use provider documentation. We queried the AFDC feeds for the Ohio example.

rows: Invariant Earth
Screen a proposed charging location with parcel, road access and electric service territory context.
Check parcel match type and road class. Ask the serving utility to confirm the connection point and capacity for your charging load.
U.S. DOE AFDC
U.S. station inventory with public access, location, connector types and installed DC fast port counts. An equipment CSV adds connector counts and rated power.
Check how station counts repeat across equipment rows and whether the station ID survives a refresh.
TomTom
Charging availability grouped by connector type and power. TomTom documents a three-minute refresh for dynamic data.
Check that both networks appear on your corridor. Measure the age of the underlying status and ask how the feed represents unknown availability.
HERE
Place search with optional connector availability, grouped by type and power. The documentation also covers equipment-level status and operator IDs.
Ask which networks expose equipment detail and usable update timestamps on your routes.
Google Places
Place records with EV connector counts and, where available, compatible-group availability, out-of-service counts and an update time.
Check how often the availability fields populate for the places you serve. Google documents how several connectors can share one charger.
Operator feed via OCPI
Operator-provided Locations, EVSEs and Connectors. The OCPI Locations module defines EVSE status and update fields.
Confirm partner access and keep the country, party, location and equipment IDs needed to match updates.

sections.heading: Two Ohio charging stops expose a 10× counting error

blocks.text: We queried AFDC for electric stations in ZIP 43140 and kept the two public locations with DC fast charging. Both sit at I-70 Exit 79. The equipment export below was captured on November 23, 2026 at 07:31 UTC. It reports equipment inventory and rated output.

rows: Pilot Travel Center 454 · 322368
Four identical rows, each listing one CCS connector rated at 350 kW. Each repeats the station count of 4.
Seven rows list one CCS connector and five list one J3400 connector. All list a 400 kW rating and repeat the station count of 12.

blocks.text: Summing the station field over the equipment rows gives 4 × 4 + 12 × 12 = 160. Counting one station total per AFDC ID gives 4 + 12 = 16. Dropping duplicate-looking CSV rows would also lose equipment detail. The four Pilot rows are identical in the export. AFDC allows an equipment row to describe more than one port or connector, so keep the three quantities separate in your data model.

The Pilot stop also shows why the kW field needs its own label. Before opening, DriveOhio specified up to 350 kW for a single vehicle. At opening, the Joint Office reported up to 175 kW per vehicle when at least four vehicles were charging. Keep the equipment rating for compatibility filters and use a separately sourced power curve or measured data for charging-time estimates.

blocks.label: Download the Ohio station records and port-count audit

sections.heading: Test the answer a driver will see

blocks.text: Suppose a driver with a J3400 inlet wants to stop at TA London. The AFDC export identifies five J3400 connectors there. The station has status E and reports 24-hour public access. That is enough to show a candidate stop. To say how many compatible chargers are free, match the station to a live feed, read the status for the compatible equipment, and retain its update time.

rows: A recent observation with compatible equipment free
Show the count, when it was observed and which connector type it covers.
A recent observation with zero free
Show that no compatible chargers are free. Distinguish ones in use from ones out of service when the feed does.
An old observation
Show when the status was last checked and offer another stop. Set the cutoff using observed delay on that network.
No status, an unknown value, or an unmatched station
Show that live status is unavailable. Keep the inventory and access hours visible.

blocks.text: For the trial, run these two station IDs and add locations from every network you expect customers to use. Compare the API with the operator’s view at the same times over a week. Log whether each station matched, whether it had a timestamp, and how old the observation was when your app received it. Include a known outage and a station with several connectors sharing one charger. Those cases reveal whether the feed can support a routing decision.

items.label: Run the same vendor evaluation across workflows
Compare port uptime, live status and actual charge success

sections.heading: How much power can a free EV charging port deliver?

blocks.text: A free port can share power with another vehicle. Check the power available to the port while its neighbors are charging, then compare it with what the vehicle can accept. California utility program site visits documented three different charging configurations in 2023. Use them to test how a routing or fleet application handles shared power.

columns: Power available in the documented configuration
What the planning tool should handle
rows: Paired public fast charger, PG&E program
Up to 125 kW for one capable vehicle or 62.5 kW per port with the pair in use.
The same available port can have a different power limit when its neighbor is occupied.
Dual-inlet heavy truck, Southern California Edison program
The charger supplies up to 90 kW per output. The truck has 120 kW and 60 kW inlet limits, giving a 150 kW combined ceiling under this fixed split.
Apply the smaller limit to each active inlet before adding the results.
Shared bus charging cabinet, San Diego Gas & Electric program
180 kW to one connector or 60 kW per connector when all three are active.
Apply the cabinet limit and the allocation the operator reports for the active connectors.

blocks.text: On the paired public charger, 30 minutes at 125 kW gives a ceiling of 62.5 kWh at the charger output. At 62.5 kW it gives 31.25 kWh. Both calculations assume a constant rate. Estimate battery energy using the vehicle’s charge curve, losses and usable plug-in time. Where the provider cannot supply a simultaneous output rating, show the listed maximum and leave the shared-power estimate unresolved.

blocks.label: Download three power-sharing configurations and five calculation checks

sections.heading: Use surrounding land and road data for expansion decisions

blocks.text: For network planning, this inventory can show where fast charging is concentrated. Invariant Earth supplies surrounding parcel and road context, including nearest major road name, road class and distance. A truck corridor study also needs the entrance location, usable turning geometry, and a route that fits the vehicle and trailer. Take a proposed load and operating schedule to the serving utility when evaluating a new site.

faqs.question: Does the AFDC API show current EV charger availability?
faqs.answer: The AFDC station status describes the facility. Use the AFDC inventory to find stations and installed ports, then use a live operator or aggregator feed for occupancy.

faqs.question: What is the difference between a charging station, an EVSE and a connector?
faqs.answer: A station is a site with charging equipment. In OCPI, one EVSE can charge one vehicle at a time. A connector is the plug or socket on that equipment. An EVSE can offer several connector types.

faqs.question: Can an available EV charger deliver less than its advertised kilowatts?
faqs.answer: Yes. A power cabinet can split its output across several active ports, and the vehicle can impose a lower limit. One California evaluation documented a paired charger that could deliver 125 kW to a single capable vehicle or 62.5 kW per port with both in use.

faqs.question: How do I count public DC fast-charging ports from AFDC?
faqs.answer: Filter electric stations by public access and DC fast charging, then sum the installed DC fast port count once per station ID. Keep equipment rows for connector detail and use a status feed for the current free count.

title: Geoforge alternatives for data center power screening
description: Compare Geoforge, Paces, PVcase, GridCARE and Invariant. Use 49 PJM upgrade records to test the dates and assumptions behind a data center power forecast.
coverAlt: Illustrative aerial view of transmission towers and a construction lane crossing harvested fields.
coverCaption: AI-generated illustration of a transmission corridor in agricultural terrain.
intro: Start with Invariant for a power study tied to the proposed campus, its load ramp and the dates each phase needs service. Compare Geoforge for candidate connections and modeled offtake, Paces for portfolio screening, PVcase Prospect for grid constraints and GridCARE for utility programs that evaluate flexible load. Give each provider the same test. Ask which facility limits service, when the relevant upgrade enters service and how a delay changes the first phase.
takeaways: In one PJM plan, the same 765 kV line segment had a June 2030 required date and an October 2031 projected date, a gap of 517 days.
AEP Ohio used separate service estimates for different groups of studied customers. One group needed an additional regional upgrade.
A usable power forecast names the connection, the case year, the limiting element and the work required for each load phase.

sections.heading: Which Geoforge alternative fits your site search?

blocks.text: The table summarizes public product descriptions. Use the Ohio example below to test what a provider can explain about its output for your location.

columns: What to ask in the demo
rows: Geoforge
Site reports with potential connections, modeled offtake by year and scenario, queue context and an energization estimate. It also offers deeper power-flow studies.
Ask which grid case and upgrade records drive the range for the first phase. Request the basis for any competing load in that case.
Paces
Regional capacity screening, project-level connection evaluation and support through interconnection studies.
Ask how capacity layer results carry into a study of your site, and which grid, land or permitting issue changes the shortlist.
PVcase Prospect
Modeled injection and withdrawal, with limiting elements for different scenarios. The published documentation distinguishes base-case and contingency coverage by market.
Check the available scenarios for your region and whether the constraint is already present before your load is added.
GridCARE
Utility work on grid capacity for flexible loads. National Grid describes its use in New York and work with UK Electricity Transmission.
Confirm the serving utility is involved and get the MW, hours, operating limits and dispatch conditions for any flexible service.
Invariant
The published site-study workflow covers AC power flow, contingency analysis, candidate connections, and indicative costs and timing.
Request the case vintage, phased results and limiting facilities. Ask which assumptions can be rerun as utility evidence changes.

sections.heading: An Ohio power forecast can contain several valid dates

blocks.text: AEP Ohio’s November 2025 study letter covered about 13 GW of new data center load. It found that the studied projects needed regional transmission work under the scenarios evaluated. Its initial estimate was Q4 2031 for Clusters 1 and 3 with the regional project and applicable parallel upgrades in service. Cluster 2 had a 2033 planning estimate and needed another regional solution. A buyer needs the customer’s actual service plan to determine which work applies.

PJM cross-references the first regional proposal, 2025W1-570, to upgrade package b4068. In the March 2026 assessment, b4068.2, the AEP portion of the Greentown to Teddy 765 kV line, had a required date of June 1, 2030 and a projected date of October 31, 2031. The first is the planning need date. The second is the forecast in that report. A particular customer’s electric service date has its own evidence.

rows: Planning need for b4068.2
June 1, 2030
Keep it as the date the reliability plan requires the work.
Projected in-service date for b4068.2
October 31, 2031
Use it as a dated component forecast and check the latest schedule.
AEP Ohio Cluster 2 service planning estimate
Check the second regional dependency, local work and actual customer schedule.

blocks.text: AEP Ohio later reported that 5,642 MW had signed binding contracts under the new tariff as of February 12, 2026. That update gives the scale of the committed cohort. It leaves the distribution by bus, year and cluster open. Ask your provider how it treats unconfirmed demand, then test a scenario with a different set of competing projects.

sections.heading: What the 49 PJM upgrade rows show

blocks.text: We extracted the required and projected dates for each b4068 sub-ID in the March assessment. Two rows projected June 2028, 21 projected October 2030, and 26 projected October 2031. These are counts of published sub-IDs. A project forecast should identify the subset the connection actually depends on.

Two rows in that assessment show an invalid calendar value in the required-date column. The February board recommendations show June 1, 2030 for both sub-IDs. The download retains the February dates and the March source values separately, with the latter normalized to null. Ask a provider which source its model used and how it handles this sort of discrepancy.

blocks.label: Download the 49 PJM upgrade rows and AEP Ohio study evidence

sections.heading: How to test the first phase before paying for a site option

blocks.text: Give the vendor the parcel, the minimum load needed on day one, the full facility load, the two service dates and how much load you can curtail. For example, ask for 50 MW by July 2030 and 200 MW by January 2032 at the meter. Those are illustrative targets, with the utility service for your project to be confirmed.

items: Ask for the modeled MW on each date at the same connection point. Record the model year, the limiting equipment and the outage assumption.
Request a second run with the relevant upgrade out of service through your target date. Ask which phase remains feasible and what changes the answer.
Get the utility’s written service terms, required work and estimated start of service. Keep energization and facility handover as separate milestones.

faqs.question: What are the best Geoforge alternatives for finding power for a data center?
faqs.answer: Consider Paces for portfolio screening, PVcase Prospect for modeled point-of-interconnection constraints, GridCARE for opportunities that depend on utility-supported load flexibility, and Invariant for a phased site study. Test your actual service dates with each provider.

faqs.question: What is the difference between required and projected in-service dates?
faqs.answer: The required date expresses when the planning case needs an upgrade. The projected date is the schedule estimate in that record. PJM’s March 2026 assessment lists June 1, 2030 and October 31, 2031 respectively for b4068.2. Use the relevant utility agreement and construction schedule to evaluate customer service.

faqs.question: Can a power screening report tell me when I can energize a data center?
faqs.answer: A power screen can estimate when the grid could support a proposed load under a specific case. The serving utility’s agreement and work plan establish the commercial service terms and estimated date. Confirm energization through a commissioning or utility record.
